rows.author: H065;
rows.title_short: Cutting Of Trees At The Foot Of Mt. Makiling
rows.abstract:
Next recognized by the Chair upon Rep. Bondoc´s
motion, Rep. Atienza of Buhay Party-List denounced the unauthorized and senseless cutting of hundreds of trees along Mount Makiling in Los
Baños, Laguna in connection with the construction of a national highway. He said that he did not allow such activities when he was the Secretary of Environment and Natural Resources. He stressed the need to protect nature which is directly linked to climate change and food security and thereafter asked for an appropriate action from the Body and government agencies concerned. (SOURCE: House Journal No.57,p.27)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-07
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Chipeco, Bataoil nad Bondoc. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: G022;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Catamco shared some personal reflections
and collective recollections on the Indigenous
Peoples´ Rights Act (IPRA) or Republic Act (RA)
No. 8371 and discussed some obstacles and
challenges to its smooth implementation. After expressing her elation over the Supreme Court´s decision upholding the constitutionality of the IPRA, Rep. Catamco argued for the protection of
the rights of the indigenous peoples (IP) specifically urging the government to give due recognition and cognizance to the 1) historical, cultural, and ethnic ties among the IPs; 2) cultural, territorial and tribal peace agreements forged through kinship and tribal
relations that are determined and held sacred by the IPs; 3) principle of plurality of ancestral domains under the IPRA; 4) role of the IPs in the selfdelineation of ancestral domains; 5) legislative enactments to realize the right of IPs to selfdetermination, defend their ancestral domains, and protect their rights; 6) review of the budget of the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP); and 7) implementation by the local government units (LGUs) of mandatory representation of the IPs in policymaking bodies and local legislative
councils. Rep. Catamco pointed out that the enactment into law of the IPRA should further realize the concerns of the IPs of their lawful rights to the social and economic development of the country. INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Jose L.
Atienza Jr. initially pointed out in his interpellation the specific violations on the rights of the IPs and the need to determine and address their concerns with regard to, as explained by Rep. Catamco, the need for delineation of ancestral domains considering that the P20 million fund provided to the NCIP was deemed insufficient to implement the purpose of the law. Rep. Atienza also rued the fact that the 17-year old IPRA Law was not being adequately
implemented and thereafter urged his colleagues to work together especially during the budget
deliberations, in addressing the plight of the IPs. INTERPELLATION OF REP. BAG-AO Rep. Kaka J. Bag-ao tackled the issuance of only one certificate of ancestral domain title (CADT) per
province. Rep. Catamco relayed the suggestion of the IPs to simplify the processing of and to augment the budget for, the CADT. Both agreed that the Committee on National Cultural Communities had to review the rules on the matter. (SOURCE: House Journal No.58,pp.7-8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-12)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Atienza and Bag-ao. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: H063;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Acedillo spoke in honor of several soldiers
who died in ambushes conducted by the New People´s Army (NPA) in Bohol in 2000 and 2003.
He cited in particular two personal friends, Lts.
Socrates Que and Ronnie Bungaos, whose wounds
showed their bravery and heroism. He remarked that the ambushers´ leader was Roy Erecre who,
ironically, was released by the military forces when he was caught in a raid in 1986. He informed the Body that Mr. Erecre was arrested the previous week and that he would oppose any efforts to include the latter and the Tiamzon
couple in the ongoing peace talks. (SOURCE: House Journal No.58,p.8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-12)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: H045;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Oaminal delved into the highly questionable
prepayment transaction for the concession fees of the government´s transmission facilities made by the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) to the Power Sector Assets and Liabilities Management Corporation (PSALM) and the ill effects of the privatization of the National Transmission Corporation (TransCo). As the Commission on Audit (COA) noted that the said
prepayment transaction blatantly infringed the
concession agreement because of the NGCP's
outstanding obligation with TransCo at the time of its privatization, he stressed that no prepayment transaction should have been allowed as it is grossly disadvantageous to the PSALM/ TransCo. He said that Congress should condone
PSALM/TransCo´s dealings with the NGCP. After
showing a comparative partial summary of the
incomes and tax payments of Transco and the NGCP,
he enumerated the special benefits being accorded to the latter, including its power to impose “passthrough” charges to the consumers. He concluded that Congress can still address the situation by revisiting the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) so that the government can regain control of the power sector and revisit the concession agreement.
(SOURCE: House JOurnal No.58,pp.8,18 & 19)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-12)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Colmenares and Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G105;
rows.abstract:
..., Rep. de Jesus correlated the significance of the celebration of Mothers´ Day last May 11 to the peace and order situation in her motherland, the Philippines, which presently faces security threats brought about by the
clandestine signing of the Enhanced Defense
Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) by the Philippine
and the United States governments. She then cited
provisions of EDCA which show how it was more in
favor of the US than the Philippines, and further
averred that like previous agreements allowing US
military presence in the country, the EDCA will
result in high social costs such as the proliferation of prostitution, sexually transmitted diseases, cases of rape and sexual exploitation, and abandoned children fathered by American service men, thus shattering the humanity and dignity of Filipino women. Rep. de Jesus then urged her colleagues to review the provisions of EDCA and other military agreements between the Philippines and the US to ascertain the disadvantageous position of the country
and at the same time, address their social costs.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 59,p.5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-13)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F103;
rows.abstract:
... the Chair recognized Rep. Agapito H. Guanlao who discussed the issues and concerns of more than three million rice farmers and other agricultural workers, which included, among others, low agricultural productivity, cheap cost of palay and corn, high production cost, inadequate daily earnings, and lack of social protection and benefits from PhilHealth insurance and the Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT)
Program. With the recent pronouncement on the critical level of water in the Angat Dam, Rep. Guanlao called on the Department of Agriculture as well as newly appointed Presidential Assistant for Food Security and Agricultural Modernization, former Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan to immeadiately release the Quick Reaction Fund for the creation of  alternative jobs to farmers who would be affected by said crisis. He also suggested that farmers who will
be affected by the drought should be included in the list of CCT beneficiaries, and the government should once again subsidize the water supply of the agricultural sector. As he lamented that there is no day dedicated for
the observance of a Farmer´s Day or Peasant´s Day
in the country, Rep. Guanlao said that he has filed House Bill No. 470 declaring May 15 of every year as National Farmers and Fisherfolk Day and thereafter urged the Members to support said measure.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 59,p.5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-13)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: C128;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Paez spoke on the issues confronting the agrarian reform beneficiaries and the contribution of agrarian multipurpose cooperatives to the economic development of their member-beneficiaries and of the country. He said that the issues included the impending June 30, 2014 deadline of the distribution
of “CARPable” lands; the determination of the
effectiveness of the agrarian reform program; and the implementation of the oversight role of government agencies to ensure the viability and sustainability of multi-purpose cooperatives through the delivery of support services.
Rep. Paez thereafter proposed the following: 1)
the passage of a one-year extension of the CARPER
law; 2) the review and proposed amendment to the
DAR Order No. 9 of the Department of Agrarian
Reform; 3) the immediate convening of the
Presidential Agrarian Reform Council to fast-track the resolution of petitions; 4) for the Cooperative Development Authority to monitor and regulate cooperatives and involve other agencies and stakeholders in enhancing the banana industry; and 5) for the Land Bank and pertinent government financial institutions to fund and rehabilitate distressed agrarian reform cooperatives.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 59,pp.5-6)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-13)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H057;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tambunting took the floor to honor the 91st
birthday celebration of her grandmother, Ms. Mila
del Sol, one of the Queens of the First Golden Age of Philippine Cinema, and also to remember the generation and culture which she helped enrich and inspire with her craft. He then recalled the humble beginnings of Ms. del Sol, her contributions to the country´s entertainment industry, and her entrepreneurial feat of being a pioneer in the janitorial service industry.
Rep. Tambunting then urged his colleagues to
craft policies that will provide jobs for the youth and the working class and that will further improve the benefits and services accorded to senior citizens under Republic Act (RA) No. 7432 or the Senior Citizens Act.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.59,p.15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-14
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Ong and Atienza; Parliamentary inquiry by Rep. Biazon. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.title_short: E D C A ( Enhanced Defense Cooperation  Agreement )
rows.abstract:
...the Chair recognized Rep. Walden F. Bello of Party-List Akbayan who agreed with the stand of the present Administration in opposing and denouncing the provocations of the People´s Republic of China (PROC) in the West Philippine Sea and supported the measures it has adopted in bringing up before the United Nations Arbitral Tribunal the rationale of the Philippine claim to the West Philippine Sea based on the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea(UNCLOS).
Rep. Bello then expressed his reasons why he
disagrees to the issue that the Enhanced Defense
Cooperation Agreement (EDCA) would make the
Chinese respect the Philippines´ rights in
Scarborough Shoal, the Spratly Islands and the 200-mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ). He argued that the EDCA would bring the country further away from a resolution of its territorial disputes with China; turn the Philippines into another of US´s frontline states like Afghanistan and Pakistan; and
move the country away from the negotiation of a
collective security agreement and increase the
volatile militarization of the area. Rep. Bello cited the following means to resolve the country´s territorial conflict with China: submit
the 1,000-page memorial delineating the Philippines´ entitlements in the West Philippine Sea to the UN Arbitral Tribunal; maximize its diplomatic option and prepare the ground for the eventual introduction of a resolution in the UN General Assembly condemning Beijing´s unilateral annexation of over 80 percent of the South China Sea; and bring a collective security agreement with the country´s ASEAN neighbors. He opined that with the approval of the EDCA, the Philippine government had lost the opportunity to forge an independent foreign policy and tarnished the important legacies of the PNoy
Administration in its antigraft and corruption
campaign and its peace agreement with the Moro
Islamic Liberation Front.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.59,pp.15-17)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-14)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Dela Cruz and Rodriguez (R.). Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
For the information of his colleagues, Rep.
Atienza said that Filipino boxer Anthony Villanueva passed away the previous day, May 13, 2014. He disclosed that Mr. Villanueva was the only Filipino who was awarded a silver medal in Olympic boxing, and underscored the importance and relevance of his life in giving honors to the country. He thereafter asked the Body to support the Resolution expressing condolence to Mr. Villanueva´s family, and also to consider Rep. Biazon´s suggestion of allocating a
certain sum of money as financial assistance to them.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-14)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
... , Rep. Dela Cruz from Party-List Abakada
focused on the various lists from different sources containing the names of several Senators and House Members who were allegedly involved in the Janet Napoles pork barrel scam. He asked why the government has allowed the justice system to dance to the tune and swing of Ms. Napoles and other whistle blowers and caused this circus to taint the integrity of the Members and degrade the House. He disclosed that he filed House Resolution No. 87, inquiring on the reported misuse of government funds such as the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF); House Resolution No. 358, inquiring on the use of the Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP); and House Resolution No. 564 inquiring on the issue of unregistered Special Allotment Release Orders (SAROs) and the government´s budgetary fund allotment under its disbursement system and
practices. In closing, he asked his colleagues to join him, through a resolution, the appointment of a special team or a special prosecutor who would solely handle the case to end the ongoing circus and allow a real investigation and inquiry on the matter.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.59,p.17)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-14)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Padilla, Atienza and Del Mar. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: C128;
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Paez related how he became a victim of an automatic teller machine (ATM) card scam in 2013 and has been awaiting a refund from his ATM card issuer bank; discussed existing policies
protecting ATM cardholders against fraud, hacking
or data theft; and urged the Body to adopt appropriate legislative action on the matter.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.60.p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-19
rows.remarks: Referrred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
..., the Chair recognized Rep. Jonathan A. Dela Cruz from Abakada Party-List who aired his serious concern on the Napoles pork barrel scam and urged the House to 1) conduct a separate investigation, preferably through the Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability, for the sake of Members who were implicated in the scam; 2) review the records properly and ferret out the truth based on the records of government agencies tasked to protect the people´s money thus preventing the House from further unfair criticisms; and 3) protect the integrity of the House as an institution and that of its Members.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.60,pp.7-8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-19
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Barzaga, Atienza, Del Mar and Paez. Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: G030;
rows.title_short: All - Women Congressional Delegation To China
rows.abstract:
Rep. De Venecia spoke about the recent 10-day
interparty visit to the People´s Republic of China (PROC) of the Association of Women Legislators Foundation composed of 12 women legislators from the House. She said that the visit was upon the invitation of the International Department of the Communist
Party of China and was a sequel to the successful
people-to-people exchange between the Philippine
Women Legislators and the Communist Party of
China, government officials, and civil society leaders in Beijing in 2012 aimed at promoting mutual respect and benefit,and joint development in the conduct of Sino-Philippine relations.
In light of the still unresolved conflict in the
West Philippine Sea and on the basis of the country´s significant blood ties and uninterrup
ted history of good neighbor relations, Rep. De Venecia proposed the creation of a Philippine-China Council to specifically address the two nations´ territorial dispute and strengthen bilateral ties and areas of common concern
and mutual benefit in trade, tourism, education,
cultural exchange, security, labor and education,
women and youth development, and mutual cooperation in the battle against climate change and environmental degradation. She further explained that the need to rebuild the bilateral relations between the Philippines and China
in view of the prospects of a better and more optimistic diplomatic, political, cultural and economic relations and the centuries of blood ties and unimpaired and continuing friendship that had started since the Tang Dynasty, far outweigh the minor irritants festering the two countries. (SOURCE: House Journal No.63,p.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-26
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep.Ong. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F093;
rows.abstract:
On the occasion of the International Day of Action for Women´s Health on May 28, Rep. Luzviminda C. Ilagan spoke on Party-List Gabriela´s particular disagreement with the privatization of the public healthcare services in the country. As enunciated and reiterated by President Benigno Simeon Aquino III in the recent World Economic Forum, she explained that the privatization of public healthcare services will affect the delivery of basic healthcare
services to the poor and marginalized sectors most particularly, the women sector, through an increase in medical costs, the absence of subsidized or free medical care, and the diminution of national appropriations for public health care. Rep. Ilagan enjoined the Members of the House to support Party-List Gabriela in preventing the privatization of public health care services and to ensure sufficient budgetary allocations for the creation of infrastructures, facilities and the remuneration for healthcare professionals. (SOURCE: House Journal No.63,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-26
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H066;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bravo delved on the government´s extended
support to Filipino farmers. He said that in observance of the Farmers´ and Fisherfolks´ Month this May, Presidential Proclamation No. 33, signed by former President Corazon Aquino on May 21, 1989, recognizes the farmers´ and fisherfolk´s role in achieving greater food production and a more equitable distribution of food resources in the country. However, he added that while farmers and fisherfolk who comprise one-third of the Philippine workforce are the government´s partners in achieving national
food sufficiency and security, they comprise the
poorest sectors in the country. Speaking on behalf of his Party-List, Rep. Bravo paid homage to farmers, fishermen and farmworkers who have been neglected over the years. He then aired his concern on the following matters, among others: 1) for the government to extend sustained support to marginalized farmers and fishermen
plagued by very high cost of agricultural production, insufficient government support and natural disasters; 2) the need to empower the farmers and fishermen by assisting the agricultural cooperatives; 3) the decrease in palay production caused by typhoon damages, moisture stress, late onset of rainfall and
late release of irrigation water; 4) shortage of
500,000 metric tons of rice even with the reported increase in the country´s rice self-sufficiency rate; and 5) the increasing rice production expenses including cost of labor, seeds, fertilizer, rental of threshers and irrigation fees. Likewise, he underscored
the threats against free trade of the forthcoming
ASEAN economic integration. He also called on his colleagues to support House Bill No. 3849, abolishing ISF, House Bill No. 3226, amending the PCIC Charter, House Bill No. 2193, seeking to amend the Agricultural Competitiveness
Enhancement Fund Law, and House Bill No. 276 or the CDA Charter Amendment Bill, strengthening the Cooperative Development Authority.(SOURCE: House Journal No. 63,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-26
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H009;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aliping spoke of the Ambient Air Pollution
(AAP) database released by the World Health Organization (WHO) which consists mainly of urban air quality data and results of ambient or outdoor air pollution monitoring for 1,600 cities from 91 countries for the years 2008-2013 which included the Cities of Baguio, Cebu and Manila. He then decried the news reports that the WHO had tagged Baguio City as the most polluted in the country. He stressed that the city´s air quality remained fresh and clean and that the WHO itself had clarified that it did not make such a baseless conclusion. He asked the agencies concerned to implement the existing laws on the environment and public health and safety, and the House to ensure adequate funds for this. (House Journal No.63,p.7-8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-26)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F048;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ong stated for the record that he did not
misuse his Priority Development Assistance Fund
(PDAF) and he had the documents to prove it; and
that those who did so should be held accountable. He however maintained that the ongoing investigations thereon were unfair, unjust and manipulative and that media coverage was disrespectful of an accused´s right to due process. Finally, he underscored the need to craft laws to prevent the misuse of public funds, and for the Members to assume their duties and responsibilities to merit the faith and confidence of the people, and regain the honor and integrity of Congress.(SOURCE: House Journal No.63,p.8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-05-26)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello spoke about the recent seizure of
power and declaration of martial law by the Royal
Thai Army in Thailand that has resulted in the arrests of people identified with the so-called Red Shirt movement and which governments worldwide have condemned. He read the statement of the Asian Parliamentarians for Human Rights which denounced the ongoing human rights abuse and aired the concern about the arbitrary detention and intimidation of hundreds of people under threat of imprisonment or fines, in that country. He stressed that the situation therein threatens democracy in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and urged the Philippine Government to condemn the coup and demand a return to democracy. In conclusion, he cited a resolution which he and some colleagues had
filed in this regard. (SOURCE: House Journal No.65,pp.3-4)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-05-28
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: G102;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Yap reported to her colleagues on her recent
trip under the auspices of the Global Legislators
Organization (GLOBE), as the head of the Philippine delegation to an international summit on climate legislation. She particularly mentioned the active participation therein of His Holiness Pope Francis and his advocacy on protecting and preserving nature and the environment. Then citing the adverse impact of Typhoon “Yolanda” which hit the country the previous year and the commencement of the rainy season anew, she proposed government action on certain issues relating to climate change. These included the following: flood control programs; allocations for the Philippine Survival Fund; creation of a standing Committee on Climate Change, as had been done in the Senate; policy reforms aligned with the development plans and needs of local government units; synchronization of different agencies concerned with the environment; and enactment of environmental laws such as the National Land Use Act and Mangrove Protection and Preservation Act. INTERPELLATION OF REP. BELLO (W.) On motion of Rep. Banal, the Chair subsequently recognized Rep. Walden S. Bello who agreed that the House should create a standing Committee on Climate Change. He and Rep. Yap also discussed the importance of civil society in the protection and preservation of the environment and the recommendation to cut down the membership of civil society in the Climate Change Commission. (SOURCE: House Journal No.66,p.17)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-06-02)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bello(W.). Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F113;
rows.abstract:
In commemorating the upcoming centennial
anniversary of the Iglesia ni Cristo (INC), Rep.
Leonen-Pizarro discussed the INC´s history from its humble beginnings to an expanding network of
followers, achievements, charity projects, global
recognition and significant contributions not only to the Filipino people but to Philippine history as well. She stated that upheld by strong foundation, unwavering belief and good leadership, the INC´s 100 years of dedication to its members and to the Filipino people has played a huge role in the history of the country, led INC members to live according to
the spiritual life that the church imparts, and guided them to become good citizens. In conclusion and on behalf of Arts, Business and
Science Professionals (ABS) Party-List, Rep.
Leonen-Pizarro expressed her support to the grand
advocacies and projects of the INC. (SOURCE: House Journal No.66,p.17)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-02
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G119;
rows.abstract:
Delivering her speech in Filipino, Rep. Cortuna
vehementlyhemently denied the baseless accusations that she had personal knowledge of Ms. Janet Napoles; had transaction with her or with anyone related to her, or had received the alleged amount of P2 million pesos from Ms. Napoles as cash advance for her 2013 Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) projects. She thereafter cited several grounds including, among others, the lack of specific details,
witnesses and pieces of evidence on her supposed
meeting with Ms. Napoles, and how the latter could have possibly met up with her when the PDAF had been suspended as early as 2013 and was later declared as unconstitutional by the high tribunal. She expressed belief that the person who masterminded her inclusion in the “Napolist” was Ms. Napoles´s present lawyer, Atty. Bruce Rivera who once filed a case against the Party-List A Teacher using his “San Beda connection” to prevent her and Rep. Mariano U. Piamonte Jr. from being proclaimed as party-list representatives during the 15th Congress.
Rep. Cortuna then called on her colleagues and
the general public to be circumspect in what they
read and see given that not everyone included in the list is truly liable. She also dared Atty. Rivera to sue her so they can determine the veracity of the allegations against her and she can defend herself against the false accusations.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.66,p.18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-02
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F030;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Garay spoke about the extinction of the
country´s forests because of illegal logging operations, particularly in the Second District of Surigao del Sur. He thereafter stressed the need to save dipterocarp trees that are good sources of hard wood but which take a long time to grow, and recommended that 1) concerned government agencies investigate and put a stop to illegal logging activities in said waterfalls
and its watershed areas; 2) his colleagues
would support the measure he authored declaring
Tinuy-an Falls and its watershed areas in his district as protected landscape, as well as another bill imposing a total log ban therein; 3) the implementation of the President´s Executive Order No. 23 be strengthened; and 4) the concerned government agencies would adopt measures that will increase the level of
awareness among the people. (SOURCE: House Journal No.67,p.9)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-06-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F069;
rows.abstract:
In behalf of the Members and her constituents,
Rep. Sy-Alvarado congratulated the Iglesia ni Cristo (INC) as it celebrates its one hundred years of existence. She underscored that the INC helped with the nation´s endeavors through its civic activities, insightful public participation and displayed its responsibility
with generosity of the Filipino spirit by helping those in dire need. She said that the INC´s guidance of its flock truly manifested the Christian life. (SOURCE: House Journal No.67,p.10)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-06-03)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F002;
rows.title_short: A I P A Summit In Myanmar
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aggabao related how in behalf of the
Speaker, he led an eight-member delegation of the
House of Representatives to the ASEAN Inter-
Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA) held in Myanmar
from May 8 to 11, 2014. He stressed the significance of how the member-nations are given the chance to exchange views and work together in promoting regional integration and building a prosperous and peaceful ASEAN community. He emphasized in particular their efforts in calling for the conclusion of a legally binding Code of Conduct in the South China Sea which was adopted in the final statement of the AIPA President, as well as the adoption of issues on
economic matters and the promotion and protection
of the rights of women and children. He hereafter
called on his colleagues to ensure that the benefits of said integration will bring about peace, development and prosperity to the peoples of the ASEAN. INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Rep. Señeres´ interpellation of Deputy Speaker
Aggabao focused on Myanmar´s form of government
and legislative process. INTERPELLATION OF REP. BELLO (W.) Rep. Bello inquired on the present political situation in Thailand, and its effect on other ASEAN members, particularly Myanmar which is moving towards a deeper democratic form of government, as well as the need for the immediate restoration of the rights of the Thai people. Rep. Aggabao stated that the political upheaval in Thailand is a setback to the idea of politically cohesive ASEAN Integrated Regional Grouping and opined that the membership of Burma to the ASEAN would also be good for the Burmese people. (SOURCE: House Journal No.67,pp.9-10)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-06-03)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps.Seneres and Bello(W.). Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G095;
rows.title_short: Reengineering The Phil. Energy Sector: Towards Reliable Power At Reasonable Rates And Cleaner By Fairly - Priced Fuel ( Reforms In Electric Power Industry )
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Reynaldo V. Umali from the Second District of Oriental Mindoro
rose on behalf of the country´s electric consumers reeling from high monthly electric bills and all concerned Filipinos suffering from the deleterious effects of oil on environment, climate change and public health. He explained that his speech seeks to enlist support to attain the objectives and full implementation of Republic Act (RA) No. 9136 or the Electric Power Industry Reform Act and RA No. 8479 or the Downstream Oil Deregulation Law, as he explained how said laws had brought about unfulfilled promises of reliable and reasonably priced
power and cleaner and fair-priced fuel to the Filipino people. Rep. Umali claimed that as Chair of the Committee on Energy for the last eight months, he had realized that while the EPIRA had laid down the groundwork for reforms in the power industry sector, the law was not able to bring about the corresponding structural and organizational requisites necessary to address the management of the power sector and the perennial and most basic problems of Filipino
electric consumers. He then informed the Body of the proposed amendments to the EPIRA Law as
contained in House Bill No. 4479, seeking to address the important concerns of the power sector based on the comprehensive and exhaustive recommendations of various stakeholders. In addition, he discussed the significance of House Bill No. 4393 or the proposed Sustainable
Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act of 2014 to
address the need for stable, reliable, efficient and sufficient supply of energy for households and industries. He also explained that the measure will provide for alternative sources of energy producing “green and clean fuel” with less impact on the environment. Thereafter, he presented a short video clip on how cetane-free diesel was able to remove the smoke from jeepneys that were used in an experiment. He
added that pollution and climate change will also be addressed and the world will recognize the country´s nationalistic, humane, pro-nature and pro-God efforts towards progress. In closing he urged his colleagues to pass the pertinent measures. (SOURCE: House Journal No. 69,pp.9 & 24)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2014-08-26
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Masongsong and Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: D034;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gatchalian alleged in his speech that Filipina nationals had been victims of human
trafficking in Malaysia and are currently confined and held in custody by the Malaysian authorities. He maintained that human trafficking has not been adequately resolved despite repeated efforts to curb human trafficking by both the Philippine and Malaysian governments. Given the criminal gravity of the offense and the substantial number of victims
in both countries, he explained that the collective efforts of the Members of Congress and pertinent government agencies and the participation of the Malaysian government are necessary to address the issue of human trafficking. He pointed out that the Philippines had already enacted into law RA No. 9208 to address the problem of trafficking in women
and children, and RA No. 10364, also known as the
Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012.
Rep. Gatchalian then urged the government through the Department of Foreign Affairs to enter into a mutual cooperation agreement with Malaysia to intensify initiatives against human trafficking facilitated by syndicates from the two neighboring countries; and to augment the present budget for the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT) and the Philippine Coast Guard so they can increase efforts in patrolling the country´s ports and seawaters.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,pp.24-25)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-09
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz brought to the attention of the
Body certain anomalies with regard to the activities in the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA) and the Bases Conversion Development Authority (BCDA), such as the conversion of thousands of hectares of land in the Clark EcoZone into a socalled “green city” and the smuggling of Indian rice into the country, as well as the usurpation of authority by certain SBMA and the BCDA officials. He urged that transparency be exercised with regard to contracts entered into or any projects worked out
by the two agencies.  (SOURCE: House Journal No. 69,p.25)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-09
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H025;
rows.abstract:
As a member of the Liberal Party (LP), Rep. Erice
took the floor to defend the honor of the LP and his party-mates from the malicious attacks perpetrated by forces committed to destroy the gains of the PNoy Administration. He claimed that Vice President Jejomar Binay and his United Nationalist Alliance (UNA) partymates Reps. Mar-Len Abigail S. Binay and Tobias “Toby” M.Tiangco have accused the LP of waging a demolition job against the Binays by linking them to the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF)
scam. Stating that while Vice President Binay has
declared that President Benigno S. Aquino III was not involved in the attacks against them, he said that the purpose is to allow Vice President Binay to continue enjoying the perks and privileges of being a Cabinet member while his family and party-mates are given the go-signal to attack the President´s political party and his
allies. He then categorically stated that the LP has no participation in the supposed demolition job and maintained that the LP is committed to contribute and support the realization of President Aquino´s legacy of good governance.
Rep. Erice concluded that it is time for the LP to defend itself from the two-faced attacks of Vice President Binay and his UNA party-mates and expose the Vice President as the epitome of an opportunistic traditional politician. (SOURCE: House Journal No.69,p.30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Bagatsing rose to deny
the accusations of Ms. Janet Napoles, in her sworn affidavit, involving him in the PDAF scam. He thereafter asked Ms. Napoles to present evidence to substantiate her allegations, and disclosed how her syndicate manipulated the Members´ PDAF without their knowledge and participation. He referred in particular to the files he got from the Commission on Audit (COA) about his alleged dealings with the Technological Livelihood and Research Center for the Masaganang Ani Para Sa Magsasaka Foundation. This, as he stressed that he never received any special allotment release order (SARO) therefor.
He emphasized that in his six terms in Congress, he was never involved in any case of graft or corruption and appealed for understanding from the media to protect his reputation and that of the others included in the so-called “Napolist” and not to brand them as thieves without evidence. (SOURCE: House Journal No.69,pp.30-31)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps.Atienza, Ocampo and Abu. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F093;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan focused on the failure of the
Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program (CARP) and
its successor, the CARP Extension with Reforms
(CARPER) Law to emancipate the peasant women
sector from the worsening social and economic
conditions and to qualify collectively as agrarian reform beneficiaries. She explained why the laws became an epic failure in implementing genuine agrarian reform in the country resulting to rising poverty, unemployment, and landlessness. Rep. Ilagan also explained the position of Gabriela Women´s Party with regard to the impending deadline of the CARPER Law for land acquisition and distribution on June 30, 2014 and their collective stand in support of House Bill No. 252 filed by Party-List Anakpawis to achieve genuine agrarian reform in lieu
of the extension of the CARPER Law.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 69,pp.31-32)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_short: Illegal Dismissal Of Nxp Union Officials
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. De Jesus criticized the unjust dismissal of the 24 officials of NXP
Semiconductors Cabuyao Incorporated Workers Union
(NXPSCIWU) last May 5, 2014. She underscored that
Gabriela Women´s Party responded to the call of the affected workers 1) because most of them were women; 2) NXP is an example of an attack to labor contractualization; and 3) to review unjust labor practices particularly inside export processing zones. She then presented to the Body the measures that aim to look into the labor policies being followed by the Philippine Economic Zone Authority, and conduct an official investigation on the matterr.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
As he focused his interpellation on the extent of
labor contractualization in the country, Rep. Señeres expressed support for Rep. De Jesus´ call for Congress to summon the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) and other local government officials to explain on the widespread practice of labor contractualization
which he said was in violation of the Constitution.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,p.32)

rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Seneres. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G001;
rows.title_short: Qualification Of City Treasurer In General Santos
rows.abstract:
Rep. Acharon delved on the provisions on Republic
Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code (LGC) of the Philippines particularly on Section 470 regarding the appointment, qualifications, power and duties of local government officials. He specifically cited the case of Atty. Jose Mariano Constantino Gonzales who was appointed by Finance Secretary Cesar Purisima as city treasurer of General Santos City but was not
accepted by the incumbent city mayor. He stressed that certain provisions in the LGC are provided to ensure checks and balances in LGUs. Considering that the appointment of a new city treasurer of General Santos City hangs on a balance thereby causing the province to lose revenues and delay the delivery of public service, he called on his colleagues to revisit Section 470 (A) of the LGC to avoid conflicting views between national and local executive officials. Deputy Speaker Padilla relinquished the Chair to Deputy Speaker Sergio A.F. Apostol.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,pp.32-33)

rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H069;
rows.title_short: C A R P E R Extension Program
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Ortega
(F.), Rep. Fernando “Ka Pando” L. Hicap from
Anakpawis Party-List focused on the plight of the
farmers and the need for a genuine land reform program in the country. He opined that after 26 years, the CARP and CARPER Laws should no longer be sustained and funded because they have failed to solve the issues of land distribution, sufficiency and rightful land ownership. He cited cases of continuous land grabbing by existing land owners throughout the country that
have resulted in labor problems and conversion of
farmlands into commercial and industrial sites through the intercession of the Department of Agrarian Reform. At this point, Deputy Speaker Apostol relinquished the Chair to Deputy Speaker Padilla. He thereafter stressed the farmers´ call to dismantle land monopoly and allow a genuine land distribution program.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,p.33)

rows.author: H063;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Acedillo spoke on the harassment by Chinese
coast guard and maritime enforcement personnel
of Filipino sailors and marines guarding the garrisons in the area of West Philippine Sea, and the appropriate courses of action that should have been undertaken by the Philippine government on the external threat posed by the People´s Republic of China (PROC) and its invasion of Philippine territories in the West Philippine Sea. He explained that the loss of
Philippine territories and the continuing external threat to Philippine national interest can be attributed to the failure of the Philippine government to embark on substantial and immediate political, diplomatic, military solutions and its failure to establish permanent
infrastructures in the contested areas and allot
the corresponding military personnel to protect these territories. He maintained that the series of preemptive actions should have formed part of a sensible and vital national security strategy to reinforce the claim of the Philippines over its territories. He then proposed that the Philippine government rely less on the results of its arbitration case before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea since its national interest is neither the national interest of the United States nor that of the international community. He maintained that the Philippine government should not leave the rest of its territories in the West Philippine Sea unprotected, undeveloped, and unmanned. He added that its previous lapses and failures in national security and lack of foresight and
action had allowed the Chinese government to establish territorial positions by invading the Scarborough Shoals in 2012 and placing in its sight further threats to other Philippine territories in the West Philippine Sea like the Reed Bank or the Recto Bank.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,p.46)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-11
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: F013;
rows.abstract:
Initially, Rep. Binay stated that her speech is in response to the recent personal attacks hurled against her and her family on the floor by people intent on promoting their own personal and vested interests. Saying she wanted to defend her family against politicking, Rep. Binay then said that the so-called white paper was baseless and Rep. Edgar R. Erice´s speech thereon merely reiterated the lies stated therein. She condemned the sowing of intrigue between her family and President Benigno S. Aquino III as she stressed that the relationship between them went beyond politics. She refuted the allegations in the speech as regards the involvement of the United Nationalist Alliance (UNA) Party and President Aquino with the white paper and the Liberal Party´s monopoly of Malacañang. On her alleged excessive Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) in 2008, she said government records would show that her allocations had always been delayed and scrutinized because her family was with the Opposition at the time; her projects had been actually implemented and properly accounted for; and the organizations involved therein had complied with requirements. Rep. Binay then urged her colleagues to act in a stately and honorable manner as the legislature is embroiled in allegations of corruption. She asked them not to permit the institution to be used in dirty
politics.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,p.48)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-06-11

rows.author: G090;
rows.abstract:
Next recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Ortega (F.), Rep. Tobias “Toby” M. Tiangco from the Lone District of Navotas City clarified that (1) he and Rep. Binay did not say that the white paper came from Malacañang; and (2) a politician was the one who gave a copy thereof to a Malacañang reporter. He opined that Rep. Erice wanted to link the Vice President to the PDAF scam and should instead file the pertinent case with the Ombudsman. He added that there was nothing wrong with members of the UNA Party joining the Majority. Finally, he challenged Rep. Erice to file a resolution asking UNA members to resign from the Majority Coalition if only to find out who would sign in its favor. This, as he pointed out that Vice President Binay
was elected by the people to work together with
President Aquino and that he has the highest approval rating among the Cabinet members.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,pp.48-49)

rows.author: F122;
rows.title_short: Performance Of The House Of Representatives For The First Regular Session Of The 16th Congress
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz spoke on the performance of the
House of Representatives for the First Regular Session of the 16th Congress. Initially, he commended the House leadership for the civil and responsible manner of undertaking the differing advocacies and concerns of the Members in the plenary proceedings that had resulted in the passage of several important measures, such as the Single Maritime Authority Bill. He stated however that the Members missed the leadership´s steadying hands and wisdom in facing the challenges which came their way during the First
Regular Session. He noted that while they were able to immediately respond to the problems of communities besieged by calamities, they were not able to face with much vigor the challenges in other fronts such as the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) issue, the power crisis, and smuggling, among others. Thereafter, he expressed hope that in the Second Regular Session, the Members would be able to respond
aggressively and with greater wisdom to the
requirements of the times.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69,pp.46-47)

rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

In his speech entitled, “A Legacy of Timeless
Reverence,” Rep. Chipeco spoke of the preparations made by his constituents for the sesquicentennial birthday of Dr. Jose P. Rizal on June 19. He then shared the story of how the tallest monument of Rizal came about, which he said, now stands as the newest tourist and historical landmark not only in the city of
Calamba, but also in the entire country.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.69, p.47)

rows.title_short: Majority And Minority Parties' Relationship; Commendating Speaker Belmonte's Leadership
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zamora stated that the Minority he represented had more often than not disagreed with the Majority on the following important issues: the constitutional amendments, the performance of the Administration in providing real, inclusive growth that the people can truly appreciate, and the failure of the government to implement a meaningful agrarian reform program. He recalled that at the start of the 16th
Congress, when he assumed the leadership of the
Minority, he promised that they would not be easy to deal with as they would ask difficult questions and look into every detail of every issue presented to the Body. He assured the Body that they had fulfilled their promise. Rep. Zamora explained that hotly-contested differences
with the Majority had sometimes resulted because of the Minority´s zeal to perform their duties.
Despite the dire circumstances that Congress
finds itself embroiled in due to controversial issues related to governance, calamities and disasters, energy problems, China´s incursion into Philippine territories, and the PDAF scandal affecting the Members, he however noted that the Minority and the Majority had still come to treat each other with respect. He pointed out that even if there were such disputes
with the Minority, Speaker Belmonte and Majority
Leader Gonzales had treated the Minority with equanimity. In closing, Rep. Zamora commended Speaker Belmonte´s strong, focused, and unwavering leadership that was apparent in reiterating the country´s national interest, in summoning the cooperation of the Members in the enactment of measures of national importance, and in successfully implementing a legislative agenda for a productive Philippines. He
underscored that the Resolution which the Body was about to consider shows unanimous support and recognition of Speaker Belmonte´s leadership of a dynamically and socially-conscious legislature. (SOURCE: House Journal No.69,p.53)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-06-11)

rows.author: A013;
rows.title_short: Closing Remarks Of Speaker Belmonte, First Regular Session, 16th Congress
rows.abstract:
With the permission of all my colleagues, allow
me to say a few words.
My esteemed colleagues:
When the 16th Congress opened a year ago, we
were riding high on the momentum of the accomplishments
of the 15th Congress.
Public gratitude for our efforts towards achieving
President PNoy´s vision of Daang Matuwid was
evident in our record-high approval and trust ratings.
The economy was growing at an unprecedented pace,
and investor confidence had never been better.
And this evening, we end the very First Regular
Session of the 16th Congress on a hopeful note.
Our committees hit the ground running from the
first day of this Congress to this hour to process and
consolidate 1,097 measures to produce 328 committee
reports for plenary action. In 71 session days, we
passed in plenary five republic acts, put on stream
for presidential approval 10 additional national bills,
approved 212 bills on Third Reading and adopted
107 resolutions. At this hour, 212 House-initiated
national bills await expeditious Senate action, 212.
True to our commitment never again to allow a
re-enacted budget, we approved the 2014 national
budget way ahead of time.
In the wake of the onslaught of natural calamities
capped by the devastating Typhoon “Yolanda,”
we approved with utmost dispatch a P14.6 billion
supplemental budget to fund critical relief and rehabilitation
programs. We also channeled funds previously
earmarked in the national budget for the PDAF
to the calamity fund by extending the validity of the
2013 Calamity and Quick Response Funds, as well
as the unreleased appropriations for operating and
maintenance expenses and capital outlays.
Among the landmark legislation we enacted to
strengthen the groundwork for inclusive growth is the
MARINA Reform and Rationalization Law to better
enforce international conventions on standards of
training for seafarers in our country.
Awaiting transmission and presidential approval
are these bills: the bill extending the life of the Philippine
National Railways to pave the way for its tooling
and development as the backbone of our public
transport system; the bill strengthening consumer
protection in the purchase of brand new vehicles or
the Lemon Law; the bill liberalizing the entry and
scope of operations of foreign banks in this country;
the bill promoting the development of micro, small
and medium-enterprises, otherwise known as the Go
Negosyo Bill; and the bill providing for the Graphic
or Picture-Based Health Warning Law on Tobacco
Products.
We made education a high priority of the Chamber.
Aware of the importance of education as a driver
of growth, we approved on Third Reading 34 education
bills, and the most notable of these are the following:
the Ladderized Education Interface Act, the
Open Distance Learning in Higher Education Act,
the Unified Student Financial Assistance System for
Higher Technical Education Act or the UNIFAST, the
Voluntary Student Loan Program of Private Banks
Act, the Open High School Systems Act, and the Free
College Education in Information and Communications
Technology Act.
We have likewise approved a bill that seeks to establish
a special education center in all public
schools divisions in the country.
We also approved the increase in the prescriptive
period from 15 to 30 years for violations of the Anti-
Graft and Corrupt Practices Act to make it more difficult
for public officials to evade public accountability.
To strengthen our agrarian, agricultural and
fisheries sectors, we approved the bills that:
1. Institutionalize credit support of the
Land Bank of the Philippines to agrarian
reform beneficiaries, farmers and fisherfolk;
2. Promote soil and water conservation
technologies for sustainable land management;
and
3. Strengthen the regulatory functions of the
Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources.
WEDNESDAY, JUNE 11, 2014 55
The landmark initiative of instituting a National
Land Use and Management Policy Act was also approved
on Third Reading to ensure judicious harnessing
and development of our land resources.
In the area of safeguarding our people´s health
and welfare, among the most notable bills we approved
on Third Reading are those which seek to:
1. Provide mandatory PhilHealth coverage
for all senior citizens;
2. Institutionalize pre-hospital emergency
medical care system;
3. Require health care facilities to provide
a price list of their healthcare services
including incidental expenses to be
charged in the medical bills of patients.
In the sphere of disaster responsiveness, we have
the Free Mobile Disaster Alerts Act, awaiting the
signature of the President, which mandates telecommunications
service providers to send free mobile
alerts in the event of natural and man-made disasters
and calamities. I am also pleased to report that the
bill modernizing the country´s weather bureau, the
PAGASA, has already been passed on Third Reading
and among its key provisions is the increase in the
pay scale and benefits of PAGASA personnel which,
hopefully, would allow us to keep our veteran
weather forecasters within Philippine shores.
I can go on enumerating what we accomplished
but let it suffice to state that the First Regular Session
of the 16th Congress bore witness to a House
that is at work despite the difficult challenges we
faced.
The work ethic we displayed gives us the impetus
and confidence to look ahead to more fruitful deliberations
and decisive action for the passage of more
strategic legislation in the Second Regular Session
and which I hope will include the following: the
Bangsamoro Law, the amendments to the economic
provisions of the Constitution, a Competition Law
that will ensure that our market is ready for the
ASEAN 2015 integration, an Anti-Dynasty Law that
does not diminish the right to suffrage while effectively
proscribing the stranglehold on political power
by a few, and a Freedom of Information Act subject
to such conditions that may be desirable, that facilitates
judicious exercise of the right to be informed of
the activities of government and its functionaries.
All these to ensure that the inroads and gains attained
towards institutionalizing good governance
and public accountability will endure beyond the
term of the present administration.
We cannot wish away nor remain silent on the
unremitting assaults to the integrity of this House
and of its Members, often without basis, in the wake
of the PDAF controversy. But this, our work in this
First Regular Session, must and should speak eloquently
for us as public servants and as Representatives
of our constituencies.
Our performance as legislators proves our fidelity
to our people´s trust. We have two years remaining
in this 16th Congress to continue to make our performance
speak for us and for this House of Representatives.
In this spirit, let us move forward to the next
regular session strengthened by our renewed resolve
to make legislation an authentic instrument of service
to the welfare of the nation and of our people.
The leadership of both houses of Congress has
been actively involved in a strong and synergetic
partnership these past months and we have likewise
pledged to continue our work in prioritizing and
shepherding legislative measures to ensure that the
performance of this 16th Congress surpasses that of
any preceding it. No scandal or controversy should
keep us from performing our functions and our duties
as duly elected Representatives of our constituencies
to the best that we can do.
On this note, may I thank the Deputy Speakers
for their hard work in the shepherding of priority
legislations, both in the committees and in plenary.
I also extend my heartfelt gratitude and commendation
to the Majority Leader and his deputies
for their able management of plenary proceedings
and facilitating expeditious action on priority bills.
To our committee chairpersons and officers, we
similarly convey to all of you our gratitude for their
unrelenting industry in winnowing legislative proposals
and hammering them into responsive pieces of
legislation.
We must also thank our esteemed Minority
Leader and his deputies for having ensured the critical
collaboration of the Minority in the passage of
vital legislative measures. Thank you.
To all of you, my colleagues, from the bottom of
my heart I can only extend my sincerest gratitude for
your unstinting hard work and unremitting cooperation.
As we celebrate tomorrow our nation´s independence
day, let us not forget that as our ancestors
have fought with blood, sweat, and tears for the Filipinos to govern themselves, so too must we fight with honesty, integraty, and solidarity so that the Filipino people may continue to enjoy the sovereignty that we all rightfully deserve. Maraming salamat sa inyong lahat. Really from the bottom of my heart, we are one House, one Congress, magsama-sama tayo at mabuhay! Maraming salamat sa inyong lahat. Thank you. (SOURCE: House Journal No. 69,pp.54-56)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-06-11)

rows.author: G085;
rows.title_short: Nominations For The Position Of The Speaker Of The House ( Speaker Feliciano R. Belmonte )
rows.abstract:
NOMINATION SPEECH OF REP. SARMIENTO (M.)
Rep. Sarmiento initially underscored the role that the 15th Congress had performed as an active partner of the President in achieving economic growth, forging domestic peace and strengthening the nation´s defenses against external threat. He however stressed that the 16th Congress still has to address many challenges, including enacting vital laws that will broaden the people´s access to good education, basic health care, and local employment opportunities. He emphasized that to meet these challenges, the House will need a Speaker who is dynamic, capable of uniting the interests of the people, familiar with the
workings of local governments, and knows how to
work in the grassroots and strengthen the frontliners of public service. As he noted the wise and fair leadership that made the last Congress significant, he nominated Rep. Feliciano Belmonte Jr. as Speaker of the House of Representatives under the 16th Congress.
SECONDING NOMINATION SPEECH OF REP. COJUANGCO (E.)
As recognized by the Presiding Officer upon Rep.
Gonzales´ (N.) motion, Rep. Enrique M. Cojuangco
seconded the nomination of Rep. Belmonte (F.) by
highlighting the latter´s outstanding characteristics as a House leader. He expressed hope that with Rep. Belmonte´s (F.) election as House Speaker, the Members will be able to accomplish their great task for the country.
SECONDING NOMINATION SPEECH OF REP. ANDAYA
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Rolando G.
Andaya Jr. emphasized Rep. Belmonte´s (F.) feat as the architect of the successful makeover of the performance of the House which passed in the
previous Congress over a thousand bills and enacted 447 laws that were described as brave, beneficial and bold. He claimed that most Members agree that it takes a leader with guts to push for the approval of such bills and a fair one to encourage free and full debates thereon.
SECONDING NOMINATION SPEECH OF REP. GARIN (S.)
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Sharon S. Garin
seconded the nomination of Rep. Belmonte (F.) as
Speaker of the House because of his fortitude in
steering the previous Congress to pass landmark
laws; his political will to conclude the 14-year old debates on the Reproductive Health Bill; his
executive aptitude that enabled the House to attain the highest public trust ratings for three consecutive years that no other Congress had ever received; and his ability to lead the Members towards the Administration´s righteous path. She concluded that the 16th Congress needs to resume, improve and expand the same path instigated by Rep. Belmonte as leader of the last Congress.
SECONDING NOMINATION SPEECH OF REP. BINAY
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Mar-Len Abigail
S. Binay opined that Rep. Belmonte (F.) possesses the leadership, character and drive that has elected him as Speaker of the 12th and 15th Congresses, and noted how he successfully balanced the passage of vital reform legislations while maintaining a harmonious
and united House. She thereafter seconded the
nomination of Rep. Belmonte as House Speaker.
SECONDING NOMINATION SPEECH OF REP. ALVAREZ (F.)
The seconding nomination speech of Rep. Franz
E. Alvarez focused on Rep. Belmonte´s track record of creating a respected, responsive and responsible House which had successfully enacted laws, appropriated funds, conducted oversight functions, and extended constituency services to the people.
SECONDING NOMINATION SPEECH OF REP. FARIÑAS
On behalf of the Nacionalista Party, Rep. Rodolfo
C. Fariñas seconded the nomination of Rep.
Belmonte (F.) as Speaker of the House because of his effective leadership of the House under the 15th Congress, especially in the areas of governmental budgeting, public accountability, public approval of the House, and national economic development. Given that 16th Congress will coincide with the final half of the six-year term of President Benigno S. Aquino III, Rep. Fariñas noted that the House of Representatives will need an effective, strong and steady leadership to sustain the nation´s progress in cooperation with the Executive Department and that Rep. Belmonte, with his personality, skills and resolve, is the right man to lead the Members of the House.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.1,pp.14-15)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-07-22)
rows.remarks: Seconding nomination speeches by Rep.Cojuangco(E.); Rep.Andaya; Rep.Garin(S.); Rep.Binay; Rep.Alvarez(F.); Rep.Farinas.

rows.author: H022;
rows.title_short: Nominations For The Position Of The Speaker Of The House ( Rep. Ronaldo B. Zamora )
rows.abstract:
NOMINATION SPEECH OF REP. CAYETANO
Rep. Cayetano pointed out that much still needs
to be done despite the accomplishments of the P-Noy government in the last three years of which the 15th Congress had been an instrumental partner. He noted the unique opportunity of the 16th Congress to influence policymaking and steer the country towards the right direction in the future but stressed that its leadership is crucial for it shall define the kind of Majority that the House will have, the Minority it will
work with, the roles they will all play, and their parts in it. For the House speakership, he nominated Rep. Ronaldo B. rows.title_short: Acceptance Speech Of Rep. Feliciano R. Belmonte As Speaker Of The House Of Representatives
rows.abstract:
ACCEPTANCE SPEECH OF SPEAKER BELMONTE
First of all, thank you very much for your
confidence in me, it is a real honor. You know the first time I was elected, I couldn´t believe it. The second time and it was the full 15th Congress, I couldn´t believe that I would last that 15th Congress, but here, you reelected me to the 16th Congress. Kaya salamat sa inyong lahat. Esteemed colleagues, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen - It is a rare honor to once more be entrusted with the speakership of this Chamber. This grave
responsibility was first reposed on me briefly in 2001, and again in the 15th Congress. Today, I am deeply humbled by your vote of confidence. I accept anew this duty equally confident that irrespective of our differing political affiliations, geographic or sectoral interest and persuasion, we will always stand strong and unified in our resolve not merely to consolidate the gains thus far realized but also to move towards our great future. I pledge before you to honor your trust with the leadership that respects the voice of every Member of this Chamber in all proceedings and upholds the
energy of this assembly as a democratic institution of government. Mula sa puso ko, maraming salamat sa inyong lahat at sa inyong pagtitiwala. At this point, I would like to congratulate the new Minority Leader, Congressman Ronaldo B. Zamora of the Lone District of San Juan, who happens to be my
neighbor actually. The Fourth District of Quezon
City adjoins the Lone District of San Juan but that is about all I know about San Juan. Whether reelected or as new Members of this Chamber, we all witnessed the backbreaking burden legislators of this House bore to discard practices of the past and steer the country towards the proverbial “matuwid na daan.” In the past three years, it was this House which overhauled the appropriation process and built the habit of the prompt enactment of a transparent and responsive national budget, this
House which refused to shirk from the politically
difficult task of impeachment, and this House which fortified the constitutional promise of accountability in government. The ratings achieved by this House in successive public trust surveys are not only historic, they are
likewise indicative of the transformation of this
institution and of our efforts to place our national constituency front, back and center of our legislative agenda. The remarkable improvements in the country´s competitive rankings, governance indicators and corruption indices; the investment credit ratings achieved under President Aquino; and the economic growth posted last year and in the first quarter of this
year which are unsurpassed in the region are
extraordinary feats which we achieved even as the
world around us grappled with a stale if not
contracting international economy and immense
political disturbances. The greatest error we can commit today is to mistake the past deeds of the past three years as ends in themselves and not merely as a preview of greater things to come. Our task in the next three years must be to resist the costly temptation of resting on our laurels, to inspire greater belief in our collective capacity for greater accomplishment within our country and outside and to marshal government resources towards making possible a more vibrant and resilient economy and people.
In close collaboration with the Senate and the
Executive, we will craft a legislative agenda that will generate greatest economic activity in our country. Economic activity that benefits the greater number; economic activity that addresses, among others, the problems of poverty, unemployment and investment. And if we stick to that goal, we will never go wrong.
Reducing the impediments to the ease of doing
business and reducing red tape even as we rationalize our incentives´ framework, meaning to say that not one or two businesses monopolizes the incentives even when they do not need them, as well as creating a more even and stable regulatory framework that will rid the private sector of its fears from funding
our economic expansion especially in such critical areas as power and energy -- and I hate to look at the Mindanao legislators in the eyes as I say those words, but definitely, we must find ways of solving the power and energy crisis particularly in Mindanao -- are essential if we are to sustain our growth and to employ the jobless. The habit of promptly enacting the national budget must be complemented by judiciousness in the use of public resources. The reprieve enjoyed by our people from additional taxes can be sustained without
substantially impairing our future growth and
expansion if efficiency in government spending is
further strengthened and institutionalized in our
Appropriations Act, and assiduously guarded through the oversight powers of this House. In the past, the oversight power has been just there. This time let us try to exercise them.
Greater investment in public infrastructure and
facilities must be encouraged, simultaneous with our concern for prudence in the use of public resources. As we pass laws that deter and close the avenues for corruption, so must we gain greater confidence in using public resources to address and anticipate the needs of our expanding economy and expanding population as well. We must nurture a legal ethos that mandates and extols prudence in spending, and transparency and accountability in the use of public funds, especially in the use of our Priority Development Assistance Funds or PDAF. Ambiguity must yield to specific, definite and verifiable development programs and projects for
both district and party-list-funded activities. Indeed, I have asked the party-list groups and I do challenge them -- to get together and come out with a plan on how to spend their PDAF because, what are the rules? Let us have them. A strict obedience to a much tightened guidelines in the use of public resources is the strongest guarantee of efficiency, ensuring that each peso spent generates exponential returns for our
people. For my part, my PDAF, since first serving as Member of this chamber in 1992 as a Congressman, were spent strictly within my district in Quezon City, subject always to public scrutiny and sometimes to public criticism. The 16th Congress coincides with the second half of President PNoy´s six-year term. These three years are sometimes more difficult to manage because whiffs of the next election hang in the air. This time might not be too different. Nevertheless, I call upon all of you, my colleagues, to unite behind this administration´s and our reform agenda in the
interest of our people so that the 16th Congress along with President Benigno S. Aquino III´s term of office, ends not with a strikeout but with a homerun or even a grand slam. Reforms in governance cannot be neglected. Government leaders must now augment our “kung walang kurap, walang mahirap” battle cry with “walang kukurap”, and marshal greater support for
the President´s agenda towards a clean, honest,
efficient and responsive public bureaucracy.
We must complete the modernization of our
institutions and the processes they adopt, and rid them of wastages which equally robs our people of essential public services. Until our accomplishments in the transformation of government become convincingly irreversible, we can neither allow our present gains to be dissipated midstream nor frustrate anew the expectations of our people. My colleagues, our beliefs and philosophies will undoubtedly require us to debate and disagree as we perform the legislative duties we will set up. But our
democratic experience in the past Congress - the
Congress which courageously tackled some of the
most controversial and divisive measures - should
remind us that our differences cannot remotely justify the obstruction of urgent and necessary legislation, but must in fact be used to enrich and improve them. With your help, ours will be a pro-active 16th Congress, one that refuses to squander the accomplishments of our predecessors but builds on them, even to surpass them, that we may finally bridge the realities of the present to the promise of our future. Ours will be a visionary Congress that will anticipate our needs and steer our economy to a path of sustained, but especially, equitable and
inclusive growth. Together with you, we will be that Congress worthy of the trust reposed upon it by the constituency who elected us - the Filipino people. Once again, maraming salamat sa inyong lahat. Mabuhay po kayo at mabuhay ang ating kaisa-isang bansa, ang bansang Pilipinas.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.1,pp.19-21)
