rows.author: A013;
rows.title_short:
Opening Remarks Of Speaker Feliciano Belmonte, Jr. Re :
Legislative Accomplishments And Plans
rows.abstract:
My dear colleagues, we open the Second Regular
Session of the 16th Congress with a profound sense of urgency. We have accomplished much in our first year but so much more needs to be done. The past four years under the leadership of President Benigno S. Aquino III witnessed remarkable growth in our economy and unprecedented transformation in the governance of our country. World Bank President Jim Yong Kim, who visited the Philippines earlier this month, referred to the Philippines as the next “Asian miracle.” He also acknowledged that our country is now a global model in fighting corruption in government. We heard the same praises from other business leaders and economic observers who attended the World Economic Forum that we hosted in May this year. Indeed, successes have been astounding in the arena of our governance. But, we face the bigger challenge of sustaining the economic growth and
consolidating the governance reforms initiated by the administration. No opportunity must be missed, no effort spared. This momentum of growth and social transformation must be sustained. In this spirit, I ask that we begin this Second Regular Session of the 16th Congress with a renewed sense of mission. We must pass legislation that will further sustain this growth, accelerate inclusive development,
and sustain the reforms for good governance
that we have achieved in the past four years.
It has been 27 years since the 1987 Constitution
was ratified and took effect. To this day, various provisions have yet to be fully operative due to the absence of relevant implementing laws. Section 26, Article II of the 1987 Constitution categorically prohibits political dynasties, but no law has been passed to implement this constitutional mandate. For the first time ever in 27 years, we have
House Bill No. 3587 or the “Act Prohibiting the Establishment of Political Dynasties” -- it is the first ever to pass Committee deliberations, and is now up for plenary discussions. We must proceed in earnest to examine the merits of this Bill and lay out the parameters of its application towards creating effective deterrents to the establishment and perpetuation of political dynasties in all levels of government. The crux of this Bill, of course, shall be how to define what is a political dynasty. Section 7, Article III of the Constitution recognizes the right of our people to information on matters of public concern. Various initiatives for a Freedom of Information Law are now pending committee deliberations. We must craft a viable FOI Law to promote greater transparency and strengthen accountability
in government, without, however, unduly
restricting the latitude of options for government action in the delivery of services to the people and in responding expeditiously to the needs of our people. There is also the clamor for a Bangsamoro Basic Law. Current realities challenge us to reexamine existing
legislative policies on the governance of certain
parts of Mindanao. The 16th Congress is given this momentous opportunity to make history by passing a responsive Bangsamoro Basic Law that shall establish a solid framework for genuine peace and enduring stability in Mindanao within the bounds of our Constitution. As soon as a draft measure is submitted to Congress, we must ensure the passage of such law. Amending restrictive economic provisions of the
Constitution that constrain the flow of important foreign direct investment in strategic sectors of our economy also demand our attention. The Resolution of both Houses on this matter is now awaiting plenary action. These proposed amendments, very simple indeed - just the intercalation of that phrase “unless otherwise provided by law”- will ensure the
continuous flow of investments that directly contribute to job creation which could liberate our people from the clutches of poverty. But, it is also necessary for these amendatory initiatives that they be simultaneously coupled with the adoption of policies supportive of the entry of foreign direct investments in this country. It is foreign direct investments, not hot money that we need. Thus, we must also act swiftly on other bills intended to create a more conducive environment for the inflow of investments, and the generation of more and better job opportunities for our people.
First, we need a National Competition Policy.
We need to send the right signals to investors who are looking for a level playing field for business. We must enact a National Competition Law that unifies, codifies, updates, and streamlines all legislation and regulations affecting competition in the country. It must complement ongoing market-oriented reforms
focusing on economic efficiency that will create competitive industries and provide quality goods and services at reasonable prices. A proposed Competition Law is now pending in the Committee level. I urge the Committee on Trade and Industry and the Committee on Economic Affairs to conclude deliberations thereon, and to submit the bill to the plenary with dispatch. Second, we must attend to the proposed Rationalization
of Fiscal Incentives Act and the Tax Incentive
Management and Transparency Act. These measures, if enacted, will send positive signals to investors who want clarity and consistency in trade and business rules and regulations. We have always been reading about remarks that
it is so difficult because the policies change all the time. So we would like to put them clearly - what are these business rules and regulations. Third, we must also prioritize measures that promote infrastructure development, foremost of which are the amendatory bills on the Build-Operate-
Transfer Law, the Cabotage Law, and the Electric
Power Industry Reform Act or EPIRA. Our country´s growth momentum is now put at
risk by the chronic precarious power supply situation. While the Executive is empowered by the EPIRA to ensure power supply security, it is incumbent upon Congress, exercising its oversight powers through the Joint Congressional Power Commission, to conduct a thorough review of the implementation of EPIRA, the rules and regulations of the Energy Regulatory Commission, and the Wholesale Electricity Spot Market or WESM. The House Committee on Energy must now consolidate proposals to address the need for competitive bidding of bilateral contracts, and of establishing a genuinely competitive power market that fosters a level playing field for all stakeholders in the industry. Fourth, we must also give focus to our nonrenewable natural resources. Extractive industries should be developed not just for private gain in the short run, but also for public benefit in the long run.
We must act in the full interest of national development and inclusive growth. We have to make sure that the mining industry, for one, yields fair and reasonable private gains but will redound to the competitiveness and efficiency of the industry. We must, however, guarantee that the government is given a
just and lawful share from the proceeds of economic activities on our natural resources, and ensure minimum damage to the environment.
We have many other vital measures in the pipeline, and I have only cited some of the key measures requiring our priority attention for this session. I say again, we still have so much to do. And I ask each one of you to help. Help ourselves do more. Recent rulings of the Supreme Court on the PDAF and the DAP have created new challenges to the legislature. PDAF, which formed part of the national government budget for decades, is now unconstitutional. Likewise, the use of savings for certain purposes through the Disbursement Acceleration Program, of which most of us were, in fact, ignorant at the time, was subject to a pending motion for reconsideration, (and was) also declared unsconstitutional. We need to explore new legislative paths to bring needed resources and services to our people. This week, after the President delivers his SONA, he will submit to us the proposed 2015 national government
budget. It is the most important piece of legislation we enact every year. We have been very supportive of the public financial
management reforms of the government in the
last four years. Without fail, we passed the General Appropriations Act on time, banishing the nightmare of reenacted budgets from the national consciousness. The prompt submission of the proposed national budget to Congress by the President, and the hard work, discipline, and commitment of every member of Congress to scrutinize and approve the budget well before the start of the next fiscal year, have made this
possible. Congress holds the power of the purse, otherwise known as the power to appropriate, and its twin, the power of legislative oversight. We must now exercise these powers in order to strengthen accountability mechanisms and ensure the proper and lawful allocation and utilization of public funds. We, Members of the House, are in unique positions of proximity to the people. In consultation with the various local development councils, we can continue
to help identify local needs and concerns that
may be overlooked by national government agencies, or which could not be addressed by our LGUs due to their limited financial resources, and we must ensure that these are identified and included in the budget. Let us also establish the framework for the conduct of continuing or year-round legislative oversight over the use of public funds by all government agencies.
With the committee system as our spearhead
beyond budget deliberations, every Committee must
now chart an oversight plan of action over departments, agencies and entities whose mandates fall within their respective jurisdictions. A year-round Committee-based oversight agenda will transform Congress into an effective horizontal accountability mechanism in our system of government, able to conduct early detection of waste, fraud, and mismanagement,
as well as institute remedial measures against acts of malfeasance in government. I have reviewed a number of COA reports, and there are two things that strike me: first, there are
large numbers of audit recommendations that are not implemented, or are only partially implemented; and second, a significant number of audit reports result only in qualified or disclaimer opinions. These indicate possible misuse of public funds or inefficient public spending. This should concern us, as representatives of the people, since we gave government the authority to collect tax money from them whom we swore to serve. In this regard, resting on the strength of the power of legislative oversight, I am directing the
Committee on Rules to study the creation of a Public Accounts and Audit Committee, with jurisdiction to call and hold to account all national government agencies, local government units, government-owned and-controlled corporations, and other government instrumentalities for their use of public funds, and to undertake legislative action to improve transparency of government operations. My dear colleagues, the tasks we face are clear - more responsive legislation for sustained growth and
inclusive development, more efficient and disciplined legislative oversight to strengthen government accountability and enhance government performance, and more resolute efforts at institutional reforms. We must continually transform the legislature into an open, accessible and effective channel for the
realization of the aspirations of our people for a better life. Together, let our collective and united efforts as one Congress mark another year of milestones for the Philippine Legislature, in service of and to the Filipino people. Maraming salamat po. Mabuhay tayong lahat dito sa Kongresong ito at ang ating bayan. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.1,pp.1-4)

Rep. Zamora, in his contra-SONA speech, pointed out that President Benigno S. Aquino III should have delivered a State of the Nation Address
that contained an outline and blueprint of the past, present, and future status of the country. He praised the gross domestic product (GDP) growth in all sectors except agriculture, the decreased fiscal deficit, the reduced interest payments, the increased international reserves, and the upgraded credit ratings. He however stressed that the rates of poverty, unemployment
and inflation remained high. He cited the need to revamp the Departments of Agriculture (DA)
and Agrarian Reform (DAR) in light of disappointing agricultural growth, corruption in the National Food Authority (NFA), rice smuggling and the Napoles scandal. In view thereof, Rep. Zamora, on behalf of the Minority, urged the PNoy Administration to consider the following proposals: 1) fast track and simplify
government procurement procedures in the Yolanda
recovery program; 2) mobilize medical and nursing
graduates as public health workers in barangay health centers; 3) encourage environment-friendly mining operations; and 4) terminate the Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) program of the government. Also, he stated that the government needs to restructure tax rates and protect consumers from monopolies and oligopolies particularly in the power, water and telecommunication sectors. Furthermore, Rep. Zamora expressed his views on the Supreme Court decision regarding the Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP), and the impeachment complaints filed in Congress against President Aquino.
Stating that a critical citizenship is most important in critical times, the Minority Leader concluded that the President could have been more forwardlooking and inspirational in his speech, and stressed that the Filipino people are hoping for a better life that they deserve.

Among other issues, he talked about graft and corruption vis-Ã -vis the billions of pesos spent for DAP projects; the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA)

rows.abstract:
In his contra-SONA speech, Rep. Dela Cruz,
speaking in Filipino, pointed out the need for
Congress to enact laws that would address the
problems of the country. He stated that the
independent Minority group had already requested
the leadership of the House to discuss the
Resolutions they have already filed to understand
better the financial standing of the government.
Rep. Dela Cruz then expressed his views on the
increasing poverty incidence in the country contrary to the claim of the government on the achievements of its Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) program. He stressed that compared to other countries, the Philippines´ income inequality and unbalanced concentration of wealth are extreme and that the poverty rate in the country remains one of the highest in Asia. Considering that the PNoy Administration is
committed to reduce poverty incidence in the
country, he suggested that the government should
redefine its policy on poverty alleviation and
reduction. While he noted the accomplishments of the PNoy Administration in the infrastructure sector, he however cited the negative impact of its privatization policy on electricity, water, and transportation rates, and oil prices. Citing excerpts from a speech of Rep. Enrique T. Garcia Jr., he discussed the need to provide local government units (LGUs) with the appropriate powers and resources that will enable them to effectively deliver basic services to the public. Finally, as he questioned the government´s claim to rice self-sufficiency as against its huge rice importation scheme for 2014; the insurgency and Bangsamoro issues; and the Administrative Code and other laws that should be realigned with the mandate of the 1987 Constitution, he called on the President
to be true to his job by leading and uniting the
Filipino people as one and observing the mandate of the law of the land. He then encouraged his colleagues to unite and work in harmony with President Benigno S. Aquino III in providing solutions to the country´s problems. He wished for equality under the Constitution, decent
living for Filipinos, and peace for all. Lastly, he appealed to the President to abide by the Constitution and do justice to every Filipino and let the people decide who will be their next leader.

Filipino people, particularly the women sector, four years after the Matuwid na Daan of the PNoy Administration has been laid down. She also noted the tragic situation of the female sector in the labor force and the increasing cases of
prostitution and violations against the rights of
women and children which are mostly brought about

foreign intervention, and removing pork barrel
and other discretionary funds as well as lump-sum
appropriations. She then asked her colleagues for
their support to its cause.

rows.abstract:
Rep. Ilagan dwelt on the countless instances of
extrajudicial killing, forced evacuation, and human rights violation that have been plaguing indigenous peoples (IPs) and their children under the PNoy Administration. As she cited August 9,2014 as the United Nations International Day for the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, she mentioned various incidents in Abra, Davao del Norte, Compostela Valley, Davao City, North Cotabato, Davao Oriental, and Misamis Oriental to show the inhumane abuse that the IPs had experienced and will continue to experience due to the militarization of their ancestral domain. She relayed their call to end such suffering, to stop allowing corporations to use military and paramilitary groups as private armies, and to resume peace negotiations between the Philippine Government and the National Democratic Front of the Philippines.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-12
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H072;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon took the floor to 1) laud the arrest of retired Major General Jovito Palparan, who was
arrested by authorities in his hideout in Sta. Mesa, Manila; and 2) condemn the illegal arrest of two youth members and organizers of Party-List
Kabataan in Central Luzon. Noting that while
General Palparan´s arrest is a momentary respite in the bleak human rights situation in the country, he lamented that the arrest of the two youth leaders is a reminder that the culture of impunity is still alive and thriving in the country. As the fight against human rights violations continue, Rep. Ridon urged his colleagues to call for the immediate prosecution of General Palparan, the immediate release of the two youth leaders and all other political prisoners languishing in prison, and for the prosecution of those who continue to
perpetuate impunity.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-12
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

principal_referral.committee: INDIGENOUS CULTURAL COMMUNITIES AND INDIGENOUS PEOPLES

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza took the floor to denounce the
implementation of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino
Program (4Ps) of the government and asked whether
the 4Ps program is really the solution to the poverty problem and not a source of corruption.
As he inquired whether the 2014 budget of the
program amounting to P64 billion would really help the poor or only benefit the few who run the
program, he stressed the need for good governance
and effective leadership to uplift the lives of the Filipino people. He denounced the program because it has failed to address the issue of extreme poverty and asked why part of its fund would be used for reproductive health projects. Finally, he said that his concern should be personally answered by Secretary Dinky Soliman of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD).
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Rep. Dela Cruz first inquired why the 4Ps has
resulted in a culture of mendicancy ... also raised concern on the following issues: 1) the DSWD´s claim that it has been consistently giving monthly allowance based on its index of the poorest among the poor and that there is a need to increase its 2015 budget; 2) the noninclusion of concerned local government units in the program; 3) the program´s goal of generating savings for use outside of its mandated tasks; and 4) the need to terminate the program so that its fund could be used for more efficient and accountable undertakings. Rep. Dela Cruz shared the views of Rep. Atienza
and promised to examine the 4Ps to avoid the abuse of government funds which have to be used properly since these are hard-earned people´s money. They also called on the Members to be careful in appropriating public funds.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,pp.10&11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-12
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.abstract:
Rep. Bagatsing explained how the truck ban and
congestion at the Port Area in Manila had adversely affected business operations, employment, traffic, and the cost of goods. He proposed that the Committee on Metro Manila Development immediately convene and hold a legislative summit for all stakeholders including local businesses, importers, exporters, truckers, brokers, shipping
companies, tax collection agencies, and consumers. He asked that his speech be referred to said Committee so that it could already address the problem.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Subsequently, the Chair recognized Rep. Jose L.
Atienza Jr. who discussed with Rep. Bagatsing the
causes of the Port Area problem as the former
expressed support for the aforementioned summit.
Rep. Bagatsing urged the City of Manila to call
for a moratorium on the truck ban ordinance
considering that it had adversely affected business operations and the delivery of goods and services to consumers. He also informed the Body that he had filed a Bill proposing a percentage share of the earnings to the host city where the ports are located. Both Members also agreed to invite the Metro Manila Development Authority (MMDA) and all other stakeholders to the proposed legislative summit
in order to really address the traffic situation in Metro Manila and find a solution that would be
beneficial to all.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.8,p.4-5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2014-08-13
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H051;
rows.title_short: House Of Representatives Electoral Tribunal Case
rows.abstract:
Rep. Reyes took the floor to question the validity of a draft resolution of the House of Representatives Electoral Tribunal (HRET) disqualifying her as a Member of the House of Representatives on the ground of her citizenship. She stated that said draft
resolution was penned by a Supreme Court Justice
closely associated with Justice Presbitero Velasco, whose son filed a case against her in the Supreme Court. She said there was a conflict of interest since Justice Velasco is the Chairperson of the HRET. She pointed out that the draft resolution of the HRET makes it possible for the Commission on Elections
(Comelec) and the Supreme Court to retroactively
annul the proclamation of a Member of Congress.
Rep. Reyes endorsed the filing of a resolution
addressed to Supreme Court Chief Justice Maria
Lourdes Sereno for the substitution of Justices
Velasco, Diosdado M. Peralta and Lucas Bersamin in the HRET. She then thanked the House members of the HRET for guarding the sanctity of the tribunal.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-26
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz rose to denounce the malpractices
and machinations abounding at the Land
Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board
(LTFRB) under the leadership of Chairperson Winston Ginez. He stressed that Chairperson Ginez has made a mockery of President Benigno S. Aquino III´s call for good governance, completely misused the powers and authority of his office to wreak havoc in the land
transportation system, issued highly questionable
circulars and decisions, and completely abandoned the basic tenets of good public service. He particularly cited the machinations in the LTFRB´s approval of the sale of the franchise of the Grand Star Coach Bus Company to Jac Liner Lucena Lines without regard to the opposition filed by Grand Star workers in the LTFRB. He suggested that the matter be investigated immediately and that said franchise be cancelled.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
In his interpellation of Rep. Dela Cruz, Rep.
Señeres stressed the need to summon LTFRB
Chairperson Ginez before the concerned House
Committees to find out if he knows the definition of “public convenience” and to ascertain that he diligently handles his task. He pointed out that Chairperson Ginez is directly under the Secretary of Transportation and Communications who should therefore be also held accountable for the actions of the former that have adversely affected the public transport system and the riding public. Finally, he expressed support to Rep. Dela Cruz´ move to file a case against the LTFRB officials concerned before the Ombudsman.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. MANALO
Rep. Manalo first inquired whether the concerned
workers of the two aforestated bus companies are
being prevented from executing a lawful judgment
issued by the court. He also sought clarification on the points that Rep. Dela Cruz has raised on the floor and whether the LTFRB has legitimized out-of-line and colorum vehicles for the sake of rationalizing the transport industry. After replying in the affirmative to the first query, Rep. Dela Cruz explained that 1) Messrs. Ginez and Corpuz should be fired from their jobs for manifestly issuing an order based on false information; 2) Congress should review the franchising system with respect to the delegation of powers and allow an overhaul of the entire land transportation system; and 3) a case should be filed against LTFRB. Rep. Manalo agreed that any government official who legitimizes a colorum bus company should be held answerable for his illegal action if found to have violated the law.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,p.11-12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-26
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Seneres and Manalo. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: H052;
rows.title_short: Death Anniversary Of The Late Sec. Jessie Robredo
rows.abstract:
In commemorating the second death anniversary
of the late Jesse Robredo, Rep. Gerona-Robredo recalled her late husband´s passion for public service, his influence on her, and her mission to keep his legacy alive. Following her husband´s example, she advocated for participatory governance which she said can
be institutionalized in local government units (LGUs) all over the country as the national government needs to share power with the people in policy and program planning, adoption, implementation, and evaluation. She stated that such was the case in the City of Naga, adding that she has filed bills institutionalizing Naga
City´s way of governance so that other LGUs can learn from it. In conclusion, Rep. Gerona-Robredo enjoined his colleagues to be role models and embrace a type of governance marked by transparency, integrity, and excellence.
REMARKS OF REP. BANAL
Rep. Banal informed the Body that both Houses of
Congress already approved on Third Reading a measure declaring August 18 of every year as Jesse Robredo Day. He stated that the late Jesse Robredo was his colleague in the Kaya Natin! Movement and was his mentor during his term as a member of the Quezon City Council which passed an ordinance similar to the Naga City Council Ordinance on participation, accountability and transparency (PAT). He remarked that the country is very grateful to Jesse Robredo for his public service.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,p.23)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-27
rows.remarks: Remarks by Rep. Banal. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: G118;
rows.title_short: Forwarding Industry; Port Congestion - Effect In The Economy - Long Term Solutions
rows.abstract:
Rep. Garin focused on the problem of port congestion in the Port of Manila that has resulted in the nonrelease and nondelivery of essential goods and raw materials; high costs of shipping and trucking; job losses; increase in food prices; decrease in trade volume; and lowered export growth rate, among others. She disagreed that the problem has been mainly caused by the truck ban being implemented by the City of Manila, this as she cited the need for long-long term solutions such as port upgrading, modernization of the Bureau of Customs, and a revision of existing customs and tariff laws. She thereafter asked her colleagues to immediately take proper action on the matter to prevent the country´s present strong economy from deteriorating and collapsing.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,p.33)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-27
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: H063;
rows.title_short: Disputed Territory; China's Presence In The West Philippine Sea; A F P Modernization Program.
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Defensor, Rep. Francisco Ashley L. Acedillo from Party-List Magdalo delved on the conflicting territorial claims and disputed territories in the West Philippine Sea, particularly the country´s Kalayaan Group of Islands (KIG) and the Scarborough Shoal, and traced the history of China´s invasion and claim of ownership over the entire area. As he cautioned against China´s build-up of military facilities since 1995 in Philippine territories, he lamented that on the contrary, the country has failed to develop any of its islands. He then proposed four basic
steps that the country can adopt to protect its territories: 1) detect the presence of airborne objects, aircraft or missiles; 2) identify them as friendly or hostile; 3) intercept and examine those not identified as friendly; and 4) neutralize those identified as hostile. He also urged Congress to pass a bill that would extend the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP)
Modernization Law for another 15 years, and to increase the AFP budget because the military is necessary in protecting the country´s maritime domain and sovereignty.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10,p.33)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-27

rows.author: G077;
rows.title_short: Death Of Seven Students Of The Bulacan State University Due To Extreme Outdoor Educational Tour
rows.abstract:
Rep. Relampagos spoke about the death of seven
students from Bulacan State University (BSU) during a field trip to Madlum Cave in San Miguel, Bulacan. He also cited similar cases of senseless loss of lives of students and teachers from different schools, colleges and universities during field and educational trips. In light thereof, he filed House Resolution No. 1397 urging the Committee on Higher and Technical Education to conduct an investigation in aid of legislation on the BSU-Madlum Cave incident to review Memorandum Order No. 17 of the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) on its standing policies and guidelines on educational
tours and field trips of college and graduate
students. After expressing his concern on the relevance, nature and costs of educational tours and field trips, and the safety of students during such activities, Rep. Relampagos argued that the compelling issue pertinent to the BSU Madlum Cave field trip is the compliance of the school and tour operators with the guidelines
set under CHED Memorandum No. 17. He subsequently
proposed for the consideration by the House
Committee on Higher and Technical Education the
several requirements that will ensure the safety of students during such outdoor educational trips. (SOURCE: House Journal No.10,p.34)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-08-27
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F102;
rows.abstract:
On behalf of Akbayan Party-List, Rep. Bello registered his protest at an arms deal between the Philippine government and the Israeli military company Elbit Systems. While the deal is supposed to enable the government to upgrade its military facilities, he stressed that it undermines the Philippine government´s position for the promotion of human rights, international
law, justice, and peace in Palestine considering
that Elbit Systems is heavily involved with the
Israeli government´s military excursions in Gaza and Lebanon which he deemed as clear and direct violations of international human rights.
Stating that he would raise the issue during the
forthcoming briefing of the Department of National Defense (DND) on the matter, Rep. Bello then urged Congress to call upon the government to scrap its deal with Elbit Sytems as the modernization of the Philippine military must not come at the expense of innocent Palestinian people.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.11,pp.5&6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-01
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: G062;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Mendoza, in recalling in Filipino the drowning and mining tragedies that happened in Madlum River in Biak-na-Bato, San Miguel, Bulacan, disclosed that several blocks of marble quarried therein had caused flash floods, but that the Office of the President has already approved the Province of Bulacan´s request to have them brought down and auctioned. He opined that the authority given to the Province was
broad and vague, and stressed that the greater portion of the marble should be used for the rehabilitation of the Biak-na-Bato to avoid the occurrence of said tragedies, and also to benefit the residents of the area. He thereafter suggested the creation of a technical committee
to ensure the proper use and disposal of the marble blocks.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.11,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-01
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Rules

rows.author: F077;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Yu spoke about the snail-paced dispensation
of justice in the killing of Mayor Ukol Talumpa of Labangan, Zamboanga del Sur and his wife Leah on December 20, 2013 at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) Terminal 3. He informed the Body that Mayor Talumpa´s fight against narco-politics had earned him the ire of narco-politicians in his town and that cost him his life. He revealed that despite the charges filed against former Labangan Mayor Kiti Nandang, who was an alleged narco-politician, and
four others for murder and multiple-frustrated murder, all the accused remain scot-free and no arrest warrants have been issued against them to date. He then called on Regional Trial Court Branch 113 of Pasay City to ensure that the alleged assassins are behind bars and urged the courts to expedite the issuance of warrants of arrest and proceed with the trial of the case.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.12,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-02
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H088;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Pagdilao spoke on the recurrence and growing
involvement of the members of the Philippine National Police (PNP) in crimes and abuses causing the people to be anxious about their safety and the security of their family members and businesses. He pointed out the need to create an environment that would be conducive to improving business and tourism. He said that the House Committee on Public Order and Safety is now tackling the PNP Reorganization and Modernization Bill to enhance the maximum potential of the police to deal with the growing sophistication and violence of criminals.
Citing the importance of public trust in the police force, he thanked and commended the annual Search for the Country´s Outstanding Policemen in Service (COPS) conducted by the Metrobank Foundation, in partnership with the Rotary Club of New Manila East, the PSBank and the PNP. He then recognized one by one the winners of this year´s COPS Search, whom he
said represent the greater number in the police force who continue to sacrifice their lives for a well-ordered society. He also acknowledged the presence in the Session Hall of the winners of Metrobank´s Search for outstanding teachers and soldiers, whom he called the present-day heroes.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BATAOIL
On motion of Rep. Monique Yasmin Q. Lagdameo,
the Chair recognized Rep. Leopoldo N. Bataoil
who initially congratulated and commended Rep. Pagdilao for his being the father of the COPS award that has evolved into what it is today, in partnership with the Metrobank Foundation that also recognized outstanding soldiers and teachers. He however lamented the incident in Lingayen, Pangasinan where a policeman went on a shooting rampage which resulted in the death of four teachers and the wounding of three others.
In light thereof, he and Rep. Pagdilao discussed
the plans that would prepare the PNP on how to deal with such problems. Rep. Bataoil then asked the type of training and recruitment systems that are needed to ensure that only men and women with stable neuro-psychiatric conditions
become members of the PNP. INTERPELLATION OF REP. BATAOIL (Continuation)Then resuming his interpellation, Rep. Bataoil discussed with Rep. Pagdilao the importance for police personnel to undertake constant training to update and
upgrade their knowledge and skills as well as to undergo the PNP transformation program to boost their spiritual well-being. He expressed belief on the need for a strong and sustained morale and spiritual recovery program for the uniformed personnel considering the nature of their work and the need for a stress management program
that should be incorporated in the training system. He then thanked the House leadership and his colleagues who extended their sympathies and condolences to the families of the victims of the Lingayen incident. 
(House Journal No.12,pp.11-12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-02
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bataoil. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H063;
rows.abstract:
In his speech on the vital contribution and exploits of the Philippine contingent to the United Nations (UN) Peacekeepers in the Golan Heights, Rep. Acedillo first explained the historical origins of the participation of the Philippines to the UN Peacekeeping Force and the deployment of Philippine armed forces to countries at war. He then described the present efforts of the Filipino UN Peacekeepers in several countries like Haiti and Liberia where they had been serving to restore and maintain the rule of law, public safety and public order; support the implementation of ceasefire agreements and peace process; and protect the UN staff, facilities and civilians. Rep. Acedillo next delved on the role of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) beginning September
of 2009 in maintaining the ceasefire between Israel and Syria, in supervising the disengagement of Israeli and Syrian forces, supervising the areas of separation, and ensuring that there are limitations observed by the two countries as provided for in a 1974 agreement on disengagement. Among others, he described the present situation of the Filipino military peacekeepers in the Golan Heights crisis, especially on their confrontation
with a Syrian rebel group linked to the alleged
terrorist group Al-Qaeda. He said that the courage which the Filipino peacekeepers have displayed are widely acknowledged by the UN in general and by the countries where they have helped preserve peace. He lamented that time and again, the safety and security of the Filipino peacekeeping troops have been threatened in the Golan Heights and in other places, some of whom have suffered injuries while others have even
sacrificed their lives. Thereafter, Rep. Acedillo underscored that together with the other Members of the House, he filed a resolution calling for a tribute to Filipino peacekeepers based in the Golan Heights. In closing, he stated that in honor of the Filipino soldiers´ efforts in the Golan Heights, the UN itself will take charge in bringing the Filipino peacekeepers back to the Philippines. He then asked his colleagues to join the delegation that
will welcome the Filipino troops as soon as they land on Philippine soil.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BELLO (W.)
On Rep. Bello´s initial concern, Rep. Acedillo
stated that vital matters such as the long chain of command from the Philippine peacekeeping contingent up to the UN Security Council as well as peacekeeping force protection and deployment, should be included among the amendments to be proposed to the UN Rules of Engagement. As regards the question of armaments for the UN
peacekeepers, Rep. Acedillo agreed with Rep. Bello that there is a need for symmetry in warfare since they are going up against rebels who do not recognize the Geneva Convention or any other international protocol that pertains to warfare.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.12,pp.12-13)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-02
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Bello. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
Thereupon, on motion of Rep. Binay, the Chair
recognized Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. from Buhay Party-List who stated that even after the Supreme Court had ruled that the Reproductive Health Law was not unconstitutional, the law has remained ineffective in the absence of implementing guidelines. He thereafter pointed to the Department of Health´s (DOH) disregard
for the ruling of the high court as it continues to implement its population control program by promoting the use of contraceptive pills. This, as he stressed that the true wealth and growth of a nation lies on its people. He refuted the government´s claim that the country has remained poor because of overpopulation, and stressed that the problem lies in the lack of good
leadership and governance. He thereafter called on his colleagues to make the DOH Secretary and the Food and Drug Administration answerable for violating the RH Law.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.13,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H057;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tambunting stressed his disappointment and
disgust at the worsening traffic in Metro Manila,
mentioning a seven-hour gridlock that had recently occurred. He said that the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) had issued a report on the country´s risk of losing P6 billion a day due to traffic as well as conducted a study, in coordination with several government agencies, on traffic-reducing
strategies. He added that despite several highway and expressway projects, traffic will not improve simply because the economy was expanding. Thereupon, Rep. Tambunting explained how the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board´s (LTFRB) no-apprehension policy of colorum buses and trucks had exacerbated the problem. Stating he was not satisfied with the explanation given by the
LTFRB Chairperson on the matter, Rep. Tambunting
expressed support to the investigation to be conducted by the Committee on Metro Manila Development into the problem. He agreed with Senator Miriam Defensor-Santiago that certain LTFRB issuances had allegedly violated land transportation laws and had added to traffic congestion in Metro Manila.
(House Journal No.14,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-08
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zarate spoke on the arrest and trial of former Major General Jovito Palparan who was accused by human rights groups of masterminding brutal killings, tortures, enforced disappearances and other forms of human rights violations committed against activists and innocent civilians. He assailed the call of former and present military officials for a special treatment for the accused as he cited the lamentable situation of prisoners in many detention centers throughout the country. He also lamented that even if General Palparan is
already behind bars, the state of impunity continues in the country as cases of extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances and illegal arrest and detention continue to rise under the PNoy Administration. He stated that General Palparan´s trial will test the
country´s justice system and the resolve of the
government to end the state of impunity in the country. In commemorating the International Day of the Disappeared, Rep. Zarate concluded that what the relatives of the victims seek is not a special treatment for the former general but to obtain justice for their lost loved ones.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.14,pp.7-8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-08
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H025;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Erice related in Filipino the various media
reports alleging that he was involved in the attempted bombing of the Ninoy Aquino International Airport last Sunday, September 7, 2014, which was presumed to be part of destabilization plans to pave the way for
Charter change (Cha-cha) and thus allow President
Benigno S. Aquino III to extend his term of office. He clarified that he was no longer pursuing the proposal to amend the political provisions of the Constitution as he would rather focus on the bills pushing for anti-political dynasty, Bangsamoro Basic Law, and freedom of information. He thereafter disclosed that some members of Anakpawis, Kabataan, Anakbayan and Makabayan staged a rally near his Caloocan City District Office condemning the
proposed Cha-cha and issuance of pork barrel, and
asking him to shut up. While he noted that the
Makabayan bloc is known to uphold the people´s right to freedom of expression, he asked whether he should not speak out on an issue that runs counter to their advocacy. Rep. Erice underscored that the President has never been involved in any case involving graft and
corruption, and that his reforms under the “Tuwid na Daan” platform eradicated graft and corruption in the government; paved the way for the investigation of the pork barrel scam; accelerated the economic growth and increased the country´s credit rating; sustained the
poverty alleviation program; focused on safeguarding the nation´s security and modernizing the military; and instituted reforms in education. He thereafter lamented how said progressive party-list bloc has been criticizing the President while continuously expressing support to Vice President Jejomar Binay, particularly on the investigation being
conducted by the Senate regarding the alleged
overpricing of the Makati Parking Building during the latter´s term as Mayor of Makati City, which he alleged was a clear case of plunder. Finally, he reiterated his support to the President, and asked whether the group has already sworn allegiance to the Vice President.
(Source: House Journal No. 15,pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-09-09)

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza opined that Rep. Gonzales was not
the most senior and most experienced legislator among them as he clarified that he was not a member of the Batasang Pambansa as he was. He also expressed support for Rep. Bagatsing´s view that the Members should have copies of the Journal and transcripts of plenary and Committee proceedings. Subsequently, he requested additional traffic aides at the main gate of
the House premises to facilitate and prioritize entry of Members´vehicles so that the Members could attend the plenary sessions on time; and urged his colleagues as well as the Speaker to give more importance to their work. (Source: House Journal No.16, p.4)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-09-10)

rows.abstract:
Rep. Bagatsing said that his six terms in Congress did not constitute a short time and asked the House leadership to return to the system of letting the chairpersons and vice-chairpersons of the Committees defend their respective measures on the floor. As he also
asked the leadership to make the Members participate in the plenary proceedings in order to come up with better and more responsive legislation, he stressed that the Body should gain the trust and confidence of their
constituents. (Source: House Journal No.16,p.4)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H080;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Señeres voiced out the clamor of the overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) against the new policy of the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC) and the Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) to integrate and collect the International Passenger Service Charge (IPSC) for terminal fee the amount of P550 into the price of airline tickets purchased online and abroad, and that the OFWs may refund it later on at counters set up by the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA). This as he said that they are exempted from the payment of travel tax and airport
terminal fee under Section 35 of the amended Migrant Workers Act and Overseas Filipino Act of 1995, otherwise known as Republic Act No. 10022.
He pointed out that the new policy created confusion and opposition from the OFWs and the members of the recruitment industry and also gave rise to speculations of misuse and corruption on the unclaimed refund in the hands of the MIAA. He strongly urged the DOTC and the MIAA to stop the said policy and to arrive at an acceptable solution without compromising the rights, convenience, and welfare of the OFWs. Otherwise, he said that he would file the necessary administrative charges to those concerned. (Source: House Journal No.16,pp.15-16)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H072;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon spoke to set the record straight on an
incident involving him and Senate President Franklin Drilon during a birthday celebration of a House colleague. He related why the Senate President was targeting him personally, citing in particular House Resolution No. 1466 which he had filed to seek an inquiry into the possible cases of corruption and overpricing involving government infrastructure projects contracted with Hilmarc´s Construction Corporation, which included the Iloilo Convention Center. He explained that he has nothing to apologize for
to the Senate President, particularly if he is merely doing his job of putting the proponents of the Iloilo Convention Center to task in view of possible cases of graft and corruption and overpricing of government infrastructure projects. He expressed hope that the requested investigation will commence soon and that the Committee on Rules will expedite the referral of
House Resolution No. 1466 to the Committee on
Public Works and Highways.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.17,pp.8-9)

rows.author: G090;
rows.title_short: List Of D A P Projects
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tiangco informed the Body that his raising a
question of quorum during the September 15, and 17, 2014 sessions was brought about by the repeated failure of DBM Secretary Florencio B. Abad to provide him on said dates the requested list of legislators who had availed of the P10 billion Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP) funds. This as he relayed to the Body the chronological details of Secretary Abad´s
commitment to provide him with the said list.
He then adverted to the list posted by the DBM in
its website which he cited as incomplete, with columns that were lacking in some data. He also explained the importance of requesting the DAP list which was to make a public and full accounting of the budgetary allocations of Congress, to include the names of Congress´
Members who had availed of the presidential
pork barrel funds and those that had been merely used as dummies to cover up for the spending of the DAP funds. Rep. Tiangco thereafter stated that he would yield to the continuation of the plenary budget deliberations, so that the budget proposal of the Judiciary could be tackled, and that he would not question the quorum anymore.
He however emphasized that Secretary Abad be given until twelve o´clock midnight to post in the website the accurate, complete, and detailed list of the DAP allocations. He then urged his peers to show support to his cause and invited everyone to check out the DBM website to verify his allegations on the DAP list. (SOURCE: House Journal No. 17,p.54)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-09-18
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.
