rows.author: C032;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Cerilles, at the outset, expressed her gratitude and that of the Members of the Committee on Welfare of Children to McDenver N. Macaraeg for singing the National Anthem and performing a doxology on that day´s plenary session. She informed the Body that McDenver is a Grade VI student at the PCCA Elementary School in Batasan Hills, Quezon City and trained by Mr. Richard T. Barbadillo. She also informed the Body that Dr. Elvira Dumalo is the PCCA
school principal. Rep. Cerilles then cited pertinent provisions of several laws and the 1987 Constitution which, among others, declare the month of October of every year as National Children´s Month, recognize the vital role of
the youth in nation-building, stipulate the rights of the Filipino child, and provide a clear mandate for child participation in building a better world. As the House has not been remiss in crafting laws for the protection of children, she pointed out that this time, the Committee has been inviting children to their
Committee meetings to consult with them on measures affecting them. She then urged the Body to include in the House Rules a provision that will allow children to be consulted during public hearings and committee meetings on matters directly affecting them. Rep. Cerilles thereafter asked her colleagues´ support for the two pending measures seeking for the protection of the Filipino child, namely, House Bills
No. 4557 and 4907. (SOURCE: House Journal No.18,p.18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-10-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H069;0000;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Hicap centered on the seemingly nonimprovement in the lives of Filipino farmers and fishermen. He then adverted to the July 3, 2014 demolition of houses of farmers and fishermen in Batangas, thus making them homeless due to a court order from the Rosario Regional Trial Court (RTC) allegedly instigated by the Laiya Development Corporation. He thereafter referred to a report he received earlier that farmers in Rodriguez, Rizal and in Hacienda Luisita, Tarlac will be forced to abandon the
lands that they have worked on for so long because of a Supreme Court decision in favor of the owners of Hacienda Doronila-Araneta and Hacienda Luisita. Moreover, Rep. Hicap adverted to the plight of farmers from San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan who are about to be displaced because of the forthcoming construction of the MRT 7. At this point, Rep Hicap pointed out that there are hundreds of farmers outside the gates of the House complex calling for the approval of House Bill No. 252 or the Genuine Agrarian Reform Bill (GARB). He then explained how the country´s agrarian reform program has failed despite much time and money spent for it.
He stressed that rampant land conversion in the
country exacerbates the farmers´ plight and endangers food production and the environment. He advocated his House Resolution No. 914 calling for an investigation of cancelled certificates of land ownership award, emancipation patents and certificates of land transfer; and also pushed for the approval of the GARB and a twin bill on national industrialization, in order to achieve social justice and economic development. Rep. Hicap thereafter dedicated his speech to two farmers from Compostela Valley who were brutally killed by military forces under Oplan Bayanihan. He
saluted the resolve and courage of such farmers and said he was honored to be part of their struggle for social justice. (SOURCE: House Journal No.18,p.18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-10-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: C128;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Paez took the floor in celebration of
Cooperatives´ Month which he said was highlighted by the recent 12th National Cooperatives Summit in Cebu City. Within the context of the International Cooperative Alliance (ICA) Blueprint 2020, he discussed the strategies that would make the cooperatives the fastest growing business model by the end of 2020 and be the acknowledged leader in
environmental, social and economic sustainability. He emphasized the role of the Philippine Cooperative Center (PCC) 2020 as the unifying and transforming voice of the movement and apex body of the cooperative sector that will promote cooperatives as the counterpart of the government. He then discussed, among others, the following matters: 1) the plans of the cooperatives in dealing with the issue of food security; 2) whether the government has the
political will to support the growth and development of cooperatives by creating a favorable policy environment; 3) the re-engineering of the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) with focus on strengthening its regulatory and supervisory powers; 4) the importance and recognition of cooperatives all
over the world; and 5) the need to integrate medium and large cooperatives and to improve their visibility and public awareness. He thereafter suggested the following: for the
CDA to propose to the Department of Budget and
Management (DBM) to allocate a budget for a
research and database project, as well as to adopt the ICA logo in all signage of cooperatives; for the PCC and the CDA to tackle the issue of capital to fund cooperative business and the cooperatives´ access to capital in their plan; for the top 400 cooperatives to
invest their surplus within the cooperative sector; and for the government to revolutionize the regulatory and development system of the cooperative sector. On behalf of the Committee on Cooperatives Development, he commended the efforts of the organizers of the recent cooperatives summit in Cebu City and acknowledged the 23,600 cooperatives all over the country on their important contributions to the country´s social and economic growth and the
prosperity of the Filipino people. (SOURCE: House Journal No.19,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-10-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: G077;
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair recognized
Rep. Rene L. Relampagos from the First District of Bohol who enumerated several accomplishments that had been undertaken for the relief and rehabilitation of the Province of Bohol after the 7.2-magnitude earthquake and devastation that had struck several of its municipalities in October, 2013. Foremost, he adverted to the enactment into law of RA No. 10634 to aid the rehabilitation of Bohol and other provinces that
had suffered the onslaught of natural disasters, the establishment of the Bohol Earthquake Assistance Fund, the efforts to update the multi-geohazard maps of the country, the rehabilitation of Bohol´s historical churches and landmarks, and the implementation of a more viable Bohol Tourism Action Plan. In view of the efforts for Bohol´s immediate and continued recovery, Rep. Relampagos expressed his gratitude for the help extended to the province and to the Boholanos by President Benigno S. Aquino III, Vice-President Jejomar Binay, Department of the Interior and Local Government Secretary Mar Roxas, Department of Social Welfare and Development Secretary Dinky Soliman, and other Cabinet Secretaries; the Members of Congress for the enactment of a supplemental budget to aid the relief, reconstruction, and rehabilitation efforts of the government; the Government Service Insurance System and the Social Security System for their calamity loan programs; the international humanitarian aid organizations; the emergency rescue personnel, and all Boholanos. Rep. Relampagos subsequently appealed to the government to re-orient its disaster mitigation programs, specifically to focus on disaster risk reduction programs rather than disaster preparedness programs to fully mitigate the adverse effects of natural calamities. (SOURCE: House Journal No.19,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-10-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H003;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Abu raised the issue of the public school
teachers in the Second Legislative District of the Province of Batangas complaining against his
supposed acquiescence in “disallowing” any salary
increase for public school teachers and stated that he has no knowledge of any such legislative measure that had been deliberated upon and approved by the House. Inasmuch as the said public school teachers may have been misled by any information on the website of the Party-List ACT Teachers, he asked Rep. Antonio L. Tinio to be more responsible and circumspect regarding the contents and dissemination of information pertaining to legislative proposals for salary increase of public school teachers. 
REMARKS OF REP. CHIPECO  Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Joaquin M. Chipeco Jr. explained that the public school teachers in his district had also complained to him about his alleged disapproval of the legislative measure allowing a salary increase for public school teachers. He claimed that he has not coauthored such measure, considering that what he had wanted is a higher salary increase for the teachers. (SOURCE: House Journal No.19,p.7)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-10-21)
rows.remarks: Remarks by Rep. Chipeco.

rows.author: G093;
rows.title_short: List Of Pro - Salary Increase For Teachers
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tinio clarified the issue regarding House Bill No. 245 providing for an increase in the salary of public school teachers from P18,500 to P25,000 and the nonteaching personnel from P9,000 to P15,000. He explained that the complaint of the public school teachers from several legislative districts could have
resulted from the posting in the website of Party-List ACT Teachers of the coauthors to the said Bill and of other names of Members who are not coauthors of the measure to entice the public school teachers into asking their Representatives to concur and support House Bill No. 245. He claimed that there were no information in the website of the names of the Members voting for the approval of the measure or any information about a voting on said Bill. He pointed out that the reason for what was posted on the website was simply to gain more support for coauthorship and not for anything
else. Rep. Tinio then apologized to the Members who were affected negatively and thereafter gave his assurance that he would personally explain to the teachers who misunderstood him.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. CASTRO
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Fredenil
“Fred” H. Castro said that in connection with Rep. Tinio´s explanation, the latter should make the necessary clarification in the website for the proper information and guidance of the teachers, as well as to assuage whatever damage it may have caused to the Members of the House.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. RAMIREZ-SATO
Coming back from her province, Rep. Ramirez-
Sato said that the teachers therein are on the verge of hating her for allegedly voting against the proposed increase in their salaries. She said that the website of Party-List ACT Teachers was very clear that those who did not sign as coauthors were identified as those who voted “no” to the said proposed Bill. She questioned the sincerity of Rep. Tinio´s apology in saying that he has made clarifications to all the regions and to all the Members affected by the misleading posting on the website because the teachers in her province have not been clarified about it. Thereupon, Rep. Ramirez-Sato said that she would move and put forward a resolution for the Committee on Ethics to investigate Rep. Tinio for putting practically all the Members in a bad light before the eyes of the teachers. (SOURCE: House Journal No. 19,pp.7 & 8)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-10-21)
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Reps. Castro and Ramirez-Sato.

rows.author: F093;
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, on motion of Rep. Banal,
Rep. Luzviminda C. Ilagan of Party-List Gabriela
spoke about the violations of international humanitarian laws committed by the Philippine Army, and thereafter urged the PNoy Administration to pursue the resumption of peace talks between the Government of the Republic of the Philippines (GRP) and the National Democratic Front (NDF). She related that during the period of sponsorship and debate on the 2015 proposed budget of the Department of National Defense (DND), she sought for a post-incident report on the alleged violations perpetrated by the 41st Infantry Battalion during its military operations in Lacub, Abra on September 4 to 5, 2014. However, she said that she was not
satisfied with the said report and for which reason she asked her staff to join the National Fact Finding and Solitary Mission organized by Karapatan in Lacub to secure witnesses´ accounts. She thereafter cited significant
findings on the deaths of Messrs. Noel Viste and
Arnold Jaramillo, Engr. Fidela Salvador and Ms.
Recca Noelle Monte. She emphasized that the families of the said persons are now invoking the rules of engagement in armed conflicts and are seeking justice through the full force of the law on crimes against humanity, specifically
Republic Act No. 9851, and the Comprehensive
Agreement on Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law. She subsequently traced the history of Lacub and its Tinguian ethnic group residents, and how they fought against development aggressions such as the entry of mining operations, megadam project and pulpwood industry. She then called for an investigation of the Lacub incident and urged the Members to adopt House Resolution No. 162, strongly urging the PNoy Administration to pursue the resumption of the GRP-NDF peace talks. (SOURCE: House Journal No.20,p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2015-02-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H066;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bravo argued on the importance of providing
new strategic directions for the future of the
cooperatives by incorporating the study of
cooperatives and cooperativism in the curriculum of the country´s educational system. He explained that the constraints to cooperative education could be attributed to the lack of understanding, and insignificant and insubstantial dissemination of
comprehensive cooperatives´ studies in the curricula of both formal and nonformal education.
He also explained that providing students with
appropriate and comprehensive knowledge of
cooperatives would ensure the future of the
cooperative movement and the long-term viability of cooperative development programs in the country. He pointed out that the most significant contribution of cooperatives to the national economy is its provision for the basic needs of far-flung communities and barangays in the form of water services, electrification,
employment, health services, agricultural facilities, and livelihood programs, which basic services had not been rendered by government.
Rep. Bravo then proposed the clustering of
cooperatives, specifically the 76% or 18,095 microcooperatives to fully maximize their potential for economic progress. He also cited the proposal by Dr. Cielito Habito for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to adopt a similar “cooperative mode” in view of the possible ramifications and opportunities that
could be had with the launching of the 2015 ASEAN
Economic Community. Furthermore, he called on the government to institutionalize the opening of a course in Cooperative Development and Administration as well as to offer baccalaureate, post baccalaureate and master´s degree programs in State universities and colleges (SUCs) that are responsive to the standards and guidelines promulgated by their boards of regents, the Commission on Higher Education and the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA). Thereafter, he enjoined his colleagues to support the passage of the bill amending the CDA Charter and all other bills that aim for the development of the cooperative sector. (SOURCE: House Journal No. 21, p.4)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-10-27
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H067;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Geron focused on the importance of
cooperatives considering that October is National
Cooperative Month. He said that the cooperative
sector remains a main driving force for national
growth and development especially in channeling and utilizing resources to attain inclusive growth. He maintained that the State continues to recognize the importance of cooperatives through the passage of laws that govern their sector, such as Republic Act (RA) No. 9520 or the Philippine Cooperative Code of 2008.
Thereafter, Rep. Geron showed a slide presentation on the breadth and depth of the
cooperative sector and presented data showing its
positive developments from 2010 to 2013, in terms of membership, value of its real property, asset value, and volume of direct and indirect employment. He emphasized that the government should institutionalize the provision to the cooperative sector of needed resources to enable it to pursue its role as a proactive provider of technology, technical assistance, training to members enterprise; as a provider of competitive interest rates in the business and assistance in insurance coverage; and as a consolidator of all production input requirements, among others.
After citing the accomplishments of the Sorosoro
Ibaba Development Cooperative (SIDC) to which he
belonged, he stressed that while the government is responding to the problems besetting cooperatives in the country, the solutions seemed insufficient. He thereafter enjoined his colleagues to support and develop strategic and long-term legislations to put an end to the struggles of cooperatives and make it easy for them to grow.  (SOURCE: House Journal No.21,pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2014-10-27)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: F103;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Guanlao talked about the recent celebration
of the World Food Day last October 16 and the state of food staples or rice self-sufficiency in the country. He said that every year, the World Food Day reminds every nation of the collective responsibility to keep humankind away from hunger, but an international report notes that one in eight people in the world is
suffering from chronic hunger. Although rice is the staple food in the country, Rep. Guanlao said that the consistent increase in its
price due to its tight supply has resulted in (1) the reduction or elimination of food items from the diet of the majority of Filipino families; and (2) rice importation despite the disadvantages brought about by double import volumes and lower import tariffs. He cited statistics in this regard. Rep. Guanlao then informed the Body that the Special Committee on Food Security, Congressional Planning and Budget Department of the House of Representatives, and experts in agriculture held discussions on policies the country must pursue towards rice self-sufficiency and thereafter enumerated their initial findings and recommendations to the Body.
He opined that these policies, along with pertinent measures he and some of his colleagues had filed, will draw the country nearest to rice self-sufficiency and food security. Citing the celebration of National Cooperative Month, he also stressed that farmers and their cooperatives play crucial roles in achieving these goals. (SOURCE: House Journal No.21,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-10-27
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H017;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Belmonte took the floor to express his grief
and outrage over the death of his friend, Mr. Arnold “AJ” Borja Jaramillo, who was killed the previous month in a so-called “encounter” between the New People´s Army (NPA) and the 41st Infantry Battalion of the Philippine Army. As he related to the Body the story of AJ as a student and later as a ranking leader of the NPA, he expressed belief that the latter did not die
but was murdered as evidence shows that he was killed in the most brutal fashion, having been gunned down in what he described as the most cowardly and treacherous manner. He thereafter referred to the autopsy reports on AJ and another casualty, Ms. Recca Noelle Monte, which
he said belied the Army´s claim of an alleged
encounter with the NPA members in Abra. He
lamented that his friend was killed in a most inhumane manner that is contrary to the provisions of International Humanitarian Law. This, as he reminded his colleagues that all these times, they have been focused on promoting peace and protecting the rights of the people. He then asked for an investigation in aid of legislation on the incidents that happened in Lacub, Abra, and for the House to exert efforts for the resumption of peace talks not only in Mindanao but throughout the nation. (SOURCE: House Journal No.21,p.6)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2015-02-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F093;
rows.title_short: Demand For The Rehabilitation Of Victims Of Human Rights Violations In Hacienda Luisita
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair next
recognized Rep. Luzviminda C. Ilagan of Gabriela
Party-List who spoke on the findings of an
international fact-finding mission 10 years after the socalled Hacienda Luisita Massacre in Tarlac which claimed the lives of seven farm workers. Initially, she said that the nation was celebrating Peasant Week in honor of the farming sector which forms the backbone of the nation. Subsequently, she relayed reports on the land distribution scheme being implemented in the
hacienda two years after a Supreme Court ruled in
favor of the farm workers, which scheme she deemed as deceitful and not based on genuine agrarian reform. Despite the Supreme Court ruling, Rep. Ilagan pointed out that vast agricultural properties remained under the names of the Cojuangco-Aquino firms and their partners and stated that they even constructed fences of barbed wires around the stashed properties in
order to stake their unlawful claim. As she cited
impunity cases from the fact-finding report, she stated that women farm workers are demanding for the rehabilitation of victims of human rights violations in Hacienda Luisita and are requesting Congress, particularly the Committees on Agrarian Reform, and Human Rights, to investigate the criminalization of agrarian disputes in order to frustrate their rights to
Hacienda Luisita lands. She also asked for an inquiry into the status of the implementation of the Supreme Court ruling and the human rights violations committed against the farm workers by security forces and private armies in Hacienda Luisita. In conclusion and in the observance of Peasant Week, Rep.Ilagan enjoined hercolleagues to support the cause of the Filipino farmers and farm workers. (SOURCE: House Journal No.18,p.19)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-10-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H057;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tambunting spoke on the recurring threat and
adverse health and medical consequences of the Ebola virus on the basis of reports from the World Health Organization (WHO) and the United States Center for Disease Control. He also talked about the preparedness of the Philippine government to address the possible onset of Ebola virus-causing diseases in the country
but raised his apprehension that the country´s public health infrastructure leaves much to be desired with regard to handling Ebola cases.
He thereafter suggested that an Ebola response coordinator be appointed just like in the US whose sole task is to ensure that Filipinos will be protected from the Ebola outbreak and who should work closely with the Task Force on Emerging Infectious Diseases which the PNoy government had created to take charge of establishing a system to identify, screen and assist Filipinos suspected or confirmed to be infected with emerging infectious diseases. Lastly, he asked the government to enlist the help of the private sector in combating the threat of Ebola disease. Expressing his belief in the tenacity of the Filipino spirit to overcome adversities, Rep. Tambunting stated
that there is no threat that cannot be blocked much less contained, if the people would remain steadfast and vigilant. He then enjoined his colleagues to take action and provide the necessary assistance in their respective
districts and to participate in the different virus-mitigating campaigns and help dissipate fears permeating in the country.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
On Rep. Atienza´s concerns, Rep. Tambunting explained where and how the Ebola virus disease started, its symptoms as well as how it is transmitted. He pointed out that there should be a focus group whose sole duty is to monitor overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) residing in Ebola-stricken countries who could possibly be infected with the Ebola virus considering that there is still no known medicine or vaccine
to cure the virus. Rep. Tambunting agreed with Rep. Atienza that the Department of Health (DOH) should lead in the dissemination of general information about the virus, and added that he would try to get pertinent literature about the subject and share it with the Members.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.24,p.11-12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-11-17
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H069;
rows.title_short: Tenth (10th) Anniversary Of Hacienda Luisita Massacre
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap relayed the
clamor for justice and genuine land reform of concerned families, farmers groups, and their local and international supporters who recently commemorated the so-called massacre of several farm workers in Hacienda Luisita in 2004. He also relayed their hurt and dismay over the speech of then Congressman Benigno S. Aquino III blaming the striking workers for the violence
that occurred, and his continuous protection of
his family´s interest over the estate. Rep. Hicap then deplored the dismissal of cases
filed against those responsible for the massacre and the assignment of some of them to high positions in the military and police forces; and the extrajudicial killings related to the strike.
Likewise, he criticized the fake and deceitful land distribution scheme being undertaken in the hacienda where the relatives of the massacre victims are not even among the list of beneficiaries. He added that the farm workers were being harassed and their harvests and properties were being bulldozed, so that they
would give up their rights to the land.
As he concluded that the quality of life of the farmers in Hacienda Luisita has not improved and the estate was still controlled by one family, Rep. Hicap challenged the Body to work towards social change and away from feudalism with the passage of House Bill No. 252 or the Genuine Agrarian Reform Bill (GARB).
(SOURCE: House Journal No.24,p.12-13)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-11-17
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps.Tinio, Seneres, Dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H064;
rows.abstract:
In commemoration of the 64th anniversary of the
Philippine Marine Corps, Rep. Alejano brought to the attention of the Members the need to fully support the strengthening of the Corps and the development of its rapid deployment and amphibious military capabilities to ensure the archipelagic territorial boundaries of the
country in the West Philippine Sea. He elaborated on its political and military beginnings and history as well
as its role in securing the archipelagic territorial boundaries of the country and in fighting Muslim secessionists and separatists in Mindanao and the communist insurgents, among others.  (SOURCE: House Journal No.24,p.14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-11-17
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H069;
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Hicap of Anakpawis Party-List discussed the national situation of the fisheries sector as he cited the celebration of World Fisheries Day on November 21, 2014 to promote and preserve fishery resources. He stressed that although the sector has vitally contributed to the economy as evidenced by various statistics, it remained to be one
of the poorest in society and a victim of social
injustice. He explained how Republic Act (RA) 8550 or the Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998 had worked against the interest of the fisheries and agricultural sector instead of reforming, uplifting, and modernizing it. He informed the Body that seafaring communities were being demolished and deprived of their source of
livelihood while foreign investors were being
protected in lake reservations. Rep. Hicap then called on Congress to repeal RA 8550, cancel the projects under the National Reclamation Plan and public-private partnership (PPP) projects of the government, stop the “No Build Zone, No Dwelling Zone” policy, implement a genuine land reform program, and object to the proposed amendments to the economic provisions of the Constitution that would only favor foreigners and not the interest of the Filipino people.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Both speaking in Filipino, Reps. Hicap and
Atienza discussed the sad state of the fisheries sector in the country particularly, the lack of livelihood and income of the fishermen and the damage brought to the river and reservoir due to aquaculture projects of building fish pens and fish cages, the dumping of waste materials by big companies, and the conversion and privatization of the fisheries sector, among others. With Rep. Hicap further enumerating the other problems confronting the fisherfolk sector, like the conversion, reclamation and privatization of marine resources, Rep. Atienza then asked the former to coauthor a resolution which he is preparing, seeking to overhaul the supervision of the fishing industry by the
Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources as well as the inspection of Laguna de Bay waters that are allegedly being ran by foreigners and big Filipino businessmen. In closing, Rep. Atienza expressed hope that the President would listen to their call to improve the lives of the fishermen and protect the country´s fisheries and
aquatic resources.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.25,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-11-18
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H065;
rows.title_short: P C O S Machines In The 2010 Election
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Atienza delved on the
questionable election returns from the precinct count optical scan (PCOS) machines as experienced in the City of Manila during the 2010 local elections. To preserve the integrity of the elections in the country, he voiced out the growing clamor among information technology (IT) experts for a manual election count at the precinct level while using electronic transmission of election results from the precinct to the municipal/city level. He also urged his colleagues to discuss, review and improve the existing electoral process in time for the 2016 national and local elections.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.25,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-11-18
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: H081;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zarate raised his concern about the
damaging, massive military operations of combat
battalions of the Armed Forces of the Philippines
(AFP) in Mindanao that caused fear and destruction in the lives and livelihood of the people particularly the Lumads; violation of the Lumads´ democratic and economic rights; and the destruction of natural resources that benefit only the foreign businesses and local counterparts. He also touched on the fifth year of the Ampatuan case as a clear illustration of the continuing state of impunity in the country; the insensitivity and out-of-touch-with-reality media statements of the President in his refusal to accept that the killings are work-related;
and the failure to achieve justice for victims of
extrajudicial killings and human rights violations because the perpetrators thereof are the security forces of the State. He then underscored that just and lasting peace can
only be achieved if the root causes of poverty,
unemployment, corruption and inequality are
genuinely resolved.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.27,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2014-11-24
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: F102;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello spoke about the questionable and
negative influences of the powerful transnational
corporations on the energy security of the Philippines, particularly Shell Corporation, Meralco and the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP). He expounded on how the current debate over the grant of emergency powers to the President should look very closely at the role of said entities.

Recognized by the Chair, on motion of Rep.
Defensor, Rep. Emmi A. De Jesus of Party-List
Gabriela spoke in Filipino about the activities held in the House of Representatives last November 20, 2014 in commemoration of the 25th Anniversary of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). She also pointed out the neoliberal policy of the
Aquino Administration on the problems of
unemployment and health care services which resulted in the increasing number of violations against children´s rights. She said that the Pantawid Pamilya Pilipino Program (4Ps) of the government is not enough to resolve these problems and urged Congress to allocate appropriate budgets for health and education to help address them.

On further motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair
recognized Rep. Luzviminda C. Ilagan, also from
Party-List Gabriela, who spoke about the increasing number of violence and rape cases against women and children in commemoration of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and the National Consciousness Day to End Violence Against Women and Children. She cited several cases of violence and rape against women, minor, and
tribeswomen by men in uniform or in authority.
She underscored that the unmitigated occurrences
of militarization and military encampments in tribal ancestral domains, residential, and school areas; extrajudicial killings; and human rights violations and abuses resulting to deaths and violence against women and children and indigenous peoples should be a cause of grave concern for the Members to whom she had sought for support in upholding the lawful rights of
and justice for the victims. In closing, Rep. Ilagan emphasized the need for a concrete resolution of human rights violations happening in the Philippines, particularly in light of
the aforesaid special days that they are
commemorating and the call for justice by victims of human rights violations and participants of the Manilakbayan march.
